SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-1 
 T&E SAFETY MANUAL 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 1 of 1 
 
All "A" General Orders dated 2024 are cancelled. 
Current "A" General Orders in Effect: 1. 
 
Change in this General Order: Reissue for 2025. 
 
 
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book T-21 Personal Protective Equipment (Safety Footwear), Item 1 Safety 
Footwear is changed to read as follows: 
Safety footwear worn must meet the standards as outlined in H&S 5350 Safety Footwear  
Procedure:  
• Meet CSA Z195 (in Canada) standard and ASTM F2413 standard (in the US and Mexico).  
• Have protective toe caps and puncture resistant soles; Note - legacy KCS employees  
have until Jan 1, 2025, to obtain safety footwear with puncture resistant soles.  
• Have 8-inch uppers as defined by the manufacturer.  
• Have a minimum 3/8-inch and a maximum 1" defined heel.  
• Be laced fully to the top.  
• Be maintained free of tears and have functioning tread.  
• Anti-slip footwear must be worn when walking on snow and/or ice.  
• Be worn at all times while on duty including deadheading (in taxi).  
Train & Engine Safety Rulebook modified accordingly 12-8-2023

sections.title: A-7 — System Ptc Rules · 2025-01-01
sections.text:
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 1 of 12 
 
All "A" General Orders dated 2024 are cancelled. 
Current "A" General Orders in Effect: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 & 7. 
 
Change in this General Order: Reissue for 2025. 
 
Due to CPKC heightened security awareness, the generic user id and pin number used for PTC Initialization 
will no longer be valid.  All emplo yees must use their unique emplo yee and pin numbers during the PTC 
Initialization process.   
   
If your unique employee and pin numbers are not working, contact your supervisor immediately for 
resolution. 
 
This General Order must be understood and discussed as part of your crew briefing.  If you have any 
questions regarding the content of this General Order, Contact your Local Supervisor. 
 
PTC General: 
All trains entering and operating in the USA must have PTC CUT IN. If the tonnage profile indicates 
PTC Disabled for CP locomotives, the PTC Help Desk must be notified before proceedin g to ascertain 
if the locomotive issue can be rectified or authorization to operate non-PTC can be granted. 
Notify the Service Operations Centre (SOC) utilizing the locomotive radio by dialing "8" as soon as 
possible, or when operating on foreign track CP crews must notify the host PTC help desk utilizing the 
locomotive radio by when one of the following conditions exist:       
a.  unable to initialize the PTC system.       
b.  experience a sync failure.        
c.  there is a PTC induced braking event.        
d.  discrepancies are found between information on a PTC display versus signal aspects in the field.       
e.  PTC is suspected of not providing a warning when it should have; or        
f.   encounter other problems with the PTC system.        
g.  If problems occur when cutting in the PTC system, the help desk must be notified immediately.       
NOTE: NEUS crews including Amtrak will use the standby channel AAR-319-453     
and then *57330# to contact the Service Operations Center.       
In the event of an enroute failure, contact the dispatcher and be governed by instructions  
received.     
NOTE: If you are unable to contact the METRA PTC Help Desk on channel 014 or AAR 033 -033, call 
out over the radio for the METRA CAD Manager.    
 
Job briefings: 
Job Briefings must include the PTC system status and any revision, modification of PTC capabilities 
and/or limitations. 
 
Transitioning to Active State: 
All PTC trains must not exceed restricted speed until the onboard system is active. The system will not 
warn, prompt or enforce any restrictions until the system is active. When the PTC System is active, all 
onboard prompts must be acknowledged to prevent enforcement. PTC must not become active within 
100 feet of a switch or signal.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 2 of 12 
 
Transfer of Authority: 
This protocol must be used where crew changes happen in TWC and Crew#1 holds a live track warrant 
and is relieved by Crew #2.   
Crew#1 parks train and engineer logs off PTC system-leaves live warrant on train as per current rules.   
Crew#2 PRIOR to pressing the INIT button the train crew must contact the dispatcher for the transfer of 
authority.    
Once the confirmation is received the transfer is completed PTC initialization can be started.    
 
Critical Feature Changes:   
On the following subdivisions: 
Ottumwa, Davenport, Marquette, Mason City, Chicago, Laredo, Canadian & Connector, Freight, C&M, 
Watertown, River, Kansas City, Tomah, Merriam Park, Withrow, St. Paul, Paynesville, Elbow Lake, 
Carrington, Portal, Detroit Lakes and Noyes, all employees must report changes  related to critical 
assets (example crossings, mile posts, signals, speed changes, switches or tracks added or 
removed…).   
Changes to critical features must be communicated through E-Request (or other designated form of 
communication as indicated by General Order) as soon as it is known and, in all cases, at least 30 days 
in advance of the proposed change. The time required is dependent on the type of change and 
proximity to other assets, no change may be made until approval from PTC Track Data is received.       
Any changes requiring immediate attention (e.g., an unplanned change or noticed by an employee) 
must be reported to the SOC or Supervisor.  
 
Restricted Speed:   
When running at restricted speed, within a yellow fence or inside a form B the following applies: If 
approaching a switch that is misaligned or is not in communication with the Onboard a "RED" fence will 
show at the switch. Within 2000 feet the onboard will display a "Switch position is Unknown" warning 
banner. The train needs to be slowed down to comply with the onboard prompting requirements. Once 
the train is within 1000 feet the switch will begin flashing and the "Switch position is Unknown" warning 
will be updated to:       
For a trailing point switch - Verify Position of Switch <Location name> is correct and a "Verified soft" 
key is provided       
or       
For a facing point switch - Indicate Alignment of Switch <Location Name> and two alignment options 
are provided. Once the route is selected or verified the red fence will clear.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 3 of 12 
 
CP trains on C&M, Elgin, and Fox Lake Subs encounter PTC difficulties, crews are   
directed to proceed as follows:     
1.  Contact MTAC (Metra’s PTC Help Desk) for technical assistance. They can be reached by 
phone at 312-322-2782, or via radio on Home Channel 14 PTC 033, or CAD Manager at 312-
322-2842 (4:00 AM to 9:00 PM).  If unable to get through to either one, call Metra Chief 
Dispatchers Office at 312-322-2844.     
2.  Provide Metra personnel at CCF with as much information and in as much detail as   
possible as to the nature of the PTC difficulties being encountered.     
3.  Based on the problems reported, Metra personnel at CCF may make suggestions as to     
specific actions the crew can take to resolve the problem(s), or may direct crews to cut   
out PTC and proceed.  In any case, if issue cannot be resolved within 5 minutes of trouble   
shooting, train crew will be instructed to cut out PTC and proceed.  The following Metra   CCF 
Employees are authorized to issue authorizations for trains to cut out PTC in CP   dispatched 
territory:  MTAC, CMTO, Train Dispatcher, Assistant Chief Train Dispatcher, Chief Train 
Dispatcher, SMTO, PM CAD/PTC and Director CCF.    
4.  If directed to cut out PTC and proceed, train may proceed without further delay,   
notifying CP C&M or Elgin Dispatcher that PTC has been cut out at first opportunity.     
As information, MTAC, CAD Manager or other CCF Personnel will also send a confirmation e-mail 
notifying CP Dispatcher that train is now operating with PTC cut out.  This DOES NOT relieve crews 
from notifying Dispatcher that train is operating with PTC cut out.  This notification   must be made to 
the Dispatcher ASAP once train is back on the move.   
 
Unauthorized Disabling of PTC: 
Unauthorized disabling of a PTC system or circumventing a PTC enforcements by manually cutting out 
the pilot valve/brake stand when not authorized is a revocable event for the locomotive engineer or 
conductor responsible and subjects any other crewmember responsible to individually liability  
proceedings, including disqualification and/or civil penalties.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 4 of 12 
 
Form B’s and TGBO’s – Effective September 16, 2024 between 0800 – 1800 Legacy CP ONLY. PTC 
subdivision files regarding Form Bs and TGBOs will be updated as follows: 
Changes 
• Onboard prompt for Form Bs will now prompt 10 minutes prior to the start time of the Form B 
(Screenshots below) 
• TGBO Clearance number will change from 5 digits to 4 digits. 
 
Form B, Active from 1445 to 1500
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 5 of 12 
 
 
Once permission is granted from the Foreman, or confirmation that train will make through the entire 
work zone limits prior to taking effect, the "Confirmed" button must be pressed.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 6 of 12 
 
 
TGBO Clearance number is changing from 5 digits to 4 digits.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 7 of 12 
 
Effective September 23, 2024 between 0800 – 1800 the attachment of Legacy KCS PTC Parameter 
files will change to CPKC combined parameters. 
 
Enter Main Track: The Onboard PTC Application (OPA) will prompt the crew when stopped at switches that 
require an enter main track (EMT) prior to entering the main track in 15 seconds.   
 
 
 
Restricted Speed: the Onboard PTC Application (OPA) will warn at 19 MPH and enforce at 21 
MPH.  Previously it was 20 MPH for warning and 22 for enforcement.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 8 of 12 
 
Freight Trains: Proceed prepared to stop at next signal, freight trains exceeding 30 MPH when approach 
signal is positively identified, must immediately reduce to a speed consistent with good train handling, 
not exceeding 30 MPH. Speed must not be increased until the next signal is positively identified as 
displaying an indication more permissive than approach (GCOR 9.8). 
Exception: Speeds within this rule do not apply to trains when operating with active PTC.  
 
 
 
Departure Test Threshold: When performing a departure test, the Onboard PTC Application (OPA) will 
reduce the air brake pressure by 26 PSI to 64 PSI from a nominal 90 PSI.   Previously it was a 20 PSI 
reduction.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 9 of 12 
 
Shoving Movements: Speed restriction 20 MPH freight trains or 30 MPH passenger trains.  
 
 
 
Delay In Active State : Upon completion of PTC Initialization prior to transitioning from Disengage 
to Active state, the Onboard PTC Application (OPA) will wait 10 seconds.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 10 of 12 
 
Work zones: Work zones are now head-end only targets, this means once the head end is outside 
the work zone, if the train comes to a stop the crew will NOT be prompted to get permission from 
Employee In Charge (EIC) to continue movement. 
   
 
 
Delayed in block: When delayed in a block in TWC-ABS territory the Onboard PTC Application 
(OPA) will NOT create a restricted speed target.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 11 of 12 
 
Delayed in block Continued, if the train reduces speed to less than 10 MPH, delayed in block will 
be invoked. The track color will change to yellow. The upper speed limit will be 19 MPH. Track will 
not have a restricted speed fence. All other functions will remain the same.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-7 
 SYSTEM PTC RULES 
 EFFECTIVE 00:01 JANUARY 1, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 12 of 12

SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-24 
 AIR BRAKE AND TRAIN HANDLING (ABTH)

General Order A-22 dated March 11, 2025 is cancelled. 
Current "A" General Orders in Effect: 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23 & 24. 
 
Change in this General Order: Locomotives left unattended (Pg. 3). 
 
 
##CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules, page 98 Section 7, 7.3, Maximum Distances Between 
Locomotive Consists will now read as follows: 
 
7.3 Maximum Distances Between Locomotive Consists 
If combined airflow to the brake pipe does not exceed 60 CFM, the maximum distance between any two 
locomotive consists is 10,000 feet.  
 
If combined airflow to the brake pipe is between 61 and 90 CFM, and no more than 60 CFM at any one 
locomotive consist, the maximum distance between any of the locomotive consist is  6,000 feet. 
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules modified accordingly (2-11-2025) 
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules, page 38 Section 3, 8.1 General Restrictions – All  
Trains will now read as follows:  
 
8.1 General Restrictions   
The following general driving axle restrictions will apply:  
• When operating at speeds below 12 mph, do not exceed the following tractive effort levels as  
indicated by the lead locomotive:  
o 135 Klbs when operating with 30 to 35 driving axles in the lead consist.  
o 110 Klbs for 36 driving axles in the lead consist.  
• Crude Oil Trains:  
o No more than 28 driving axles are permitted in the lead consist of loaded conventional 
crude oil trains.  
o No more than 24 driving axles are permitted in the lead consist of loaded conventional 
crude oil trains handling DOT 111 tank cars.  
• No more than 16 driving axles are permitted on trains operating over tracks where 6 axle  
locomotives are prohibited.  
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules modified accordingly (11-20-2024) 
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules, page 38 Section 3, 8.2 Driving Axles Limitations –  
Conventional Trains will now read as follows:  
 
8.2 Driving Axle Limitations – Conventional Trains  
Unless otherwise specified by timetable or this section, a conventional train must not exceed 30 driving 
axles. The following exceptions apply:  
 
TrAM Areas 1, 2, and 3  
Trains are permitted to operate with up to 36 driving axles when the following conditions are met:  
• The head 15 cars must weigh at least 50 tons.  
• When multi-platform cars are part of the head 15 cars, no platforms can be empty and the average 
weight of all platforms on each car must be 50 tons or more.  
 
TrAM Areas 4, 5, and 6  
The following driving axle requirements will apply:  
• Do not exceed 24 driving axles.  
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules modified accordingly (11-20-2024)

8.3 Driving Axle Limitations – Distributed Power Trains  
The maximum number of driving axles permitted on distributed power trains are as follows:  
TrAM Areas 1, 2, and 3 TrAM Areas 4, 5, and 6  
• Lead Consist: 30.

position, and 1 locomotive at the rear of the train. Examples: 2 -1-1, 2-1-0, 2-0-1, 1-1-1, 1-0-1, 1-1-0.  Exception: 2 -0-1 
and 1-0-1 configurations are not permitted on the Haverty subdivision  
1. Applies to a maximum of 2,460 tons per locomotive, to a maximum of 139 cars.

3. Summer only account brake pipe gradient in colder temperatures.  
4. Applies to sand trains only.  
5. Applicable on the US Southern Region only between Kansas City and Laredo. No empty cars are

##CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules, Page 52, Section 4, 5.2 Leaving Locomotives Unattended, 
Baton Rouge is added to the list of yards or terminals with 24-hour oversight. 
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules modified accordingly (3-11-2025) 
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules, page 62 Section 5, 8.2 Braking Limitations . While in a 
Temporary Speed restriction, one half mile is changed to one mile and will now read as follows: 
 
8.2 Dynamic Brake Limitations 
Dynamic brake limits refer to the effort value, Klbs or amps, displayed on the lead locomotive gauge or 
screen. Do not exceed a dynamic brake factor of 20 on any locomotive consist. If the dynamic brake must 
be cut out on a locomotive without a cut out switch, the locomotive must be isolated. 
 
The following will apply when the dynamic brake factor of the lead locomotive consist is  
10 or greater: 
• When operating on other than main track, or any track with a maximum speed of 15 mph or less, 
the DB effort must not exceed 60 Klbs (AC) or 500 amps (DC). 
 
• When operating through any turnout, the DB effort must not exceed 60 Klbs or 500 amps (DC): 
o Conventional trains: Prior to the turnout, and until at least half the movement has passed the 
turnout. 
o Distributed Power trains: prior to the turnout, and until the entire movement has passed the 
turnout.  
 
• When governed by a temporary speed restriction, the DB effort must not exceed 40 Klbs (AC) or 
350 amps (DC): 
o Conventional trains: one mile prior to the restriction, and until the locomotive(s) are clear of the 
restriction. 
o Distributed Power trains: one mile prior to the restriction, and until the entire movement is clear 
of the restriction. 
o Exception: when any portion of such restriction is on a Heavy or Mountain grade, the DB effort 
must not exceed 60 Klbs (AC) or 500 amps (DC). 
• When governed by a Heat Slow restriction, the DB effort must not exceed 60 Klbs (AC) or 500 
amps (DC) until the entire movement is clear of the restriction. 
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules modified accordingly (8-1-2024) 
 
CPKC Air Brake and Train Handling Rules, page 83, Section 7, 2.2 Conditioning Remote  
Locomotive(s), under Control Stand, Engine Run and Generator Field switch positions will now  
will now read: 
   
o Engine Run – On.  
o Generator Field – Off.

sections.title: A-27 — System Locomotive Technical Info · 2025-04-04
sections.text:
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-27 
 SYSTEM LOCOMOTIVE TECHNICAL INFO 
 APRIL 4, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 1 of 6 
 
General Order A-3 dated January 1, 2025, and A-26 dated April 4, 2025 are cancelled. 
Current "A" General Orders in Effect: 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 15, 19, 20, 23, 24, 25 & 27. 
 
Change in this General Order: Update to FTO information (Pgs. 2 & 4). 
 
 
RCL Man Down Toggle Switch Installations  
To eliminate the need for cable interchanges at the locomotive radio, remote control locomotives 
across the network are being equipped with a RCL Man Down toggle switch. This toggle switch will be 
located on the side of the control stand and operates as follows:  
• Manual Mode (upper position) – connects the conductor handset to the locomotive radio  
• Middle position – not used  
• RCL Mode (lower position) – connects the RCL Man Down System to the locomotive radio  
Where equipped, the RCL Man Down toggle switch must be set to RCL mode during remote control 
operation and Manual Mode when the locomotive will be left or used in conventional operation.   
 
  
 
Distributed Power PCS Recovery Feature  
CP’s Distributed Power software is being modified to include a new feature that recovers the PCS and 
applies full independent brake cylinder pressure on remote(s) (or Lead in Tower Mode) during 
emergency and penalty brake applications.  Once this occurs, the remote(s) will respond to dynamic 
brake commands initiated by the lead locomotive control stand, even if the lead locomotive is still in 
Emergency.  
How it works  
60 seconds after an emergency or penalty brake application is initiated, the PCS will recover, the alarm 
will extinguish, and independent brake will fully apply on the affected remote(s).  If the train was moving 
at the time of the emergency or penalty brake application and it takes longer than 60 seconds for the 
remote(s) to come to a stop, the PCS will recover and the alarm will extinguish after the remote(s) stop. 
After a penalty brake application, the remote Brake Valve will remain IN unless it has been  
commanded OUT by the Locomotive Engineer, as has always been the case.  
• Example 1: Remote(s) stop 40 seconds after emergency, the PCS alarm will extinguish  60 
seconds after the emergency brake application (in this example, 20 seconds after stopping).  
• Example 2: Remote(s) stop 80 seconds after emergency, the PCS alarm will extinguish  
after the remote(s) stop.  
• Example 3: After uncoupling and the remote(s) are left standing in emergency, the PCS  
alarm will extinguish 60 seconds after the emergency brake application.  
In the examples above, once the PCS alarm has extinguished and the independent brake is fully 
applied, the Brake Valve will remain OUT on the affected remote(s). If the PCS does not recover as 
described due to the Locomotives upgrade status, be governed by existing instructions.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-27 
 SYSTEM LOCOMOTIVE TECHNICAL INFO 
 APRIL 4, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 2 of 6 
 
Test Equipment on CP 7034 and CP 8077  
An engineer’s instrument camera is installed on locomotives CP 7034 and CP 8077. In -cab 
microphones have been installed for placement and functionality testing. These locomotives will be 
operated in both Lead and Trail in the United States and Canada and will not require any special action 
from train and engine employees. Recordings will only be reviewed by authorized technicians in the 
Locomotive Systems Department, and only for the purposes of optimizing system operation. Recorded 
in-cab video and audio from the Engineer’s instrument camera will not be used for any other purpose 
whatsoever. All instrument camera and in-cab audio recordings will be destroyed after testing 
completes. 
 
Enhanced Trip Optimizer and ABTH Section 7, Item 7.2  
Trip Optimizer utilizes an algorithm to determine how the auto control will function with remote 
locomotives in both synchronous (same as lead) and asynchronous (independent) mode. It 
examines the train consist (loads, empties, car types, remote placement, etc.), which can be 
updated "on the fly" to accommodate for over-the-road switching. It also utilizes a detailed GPS 
profile of the track grade to determine the location of each locomotive, including remotes, and 
adjusts every locomotive for changes in grade.   
 
Remote consists will operate independent of each other when in Enhanced Auto Independent 
mode. This may result in one or more consists operating in Dynamic Braking while others are 
producing tractive effort – this is intentional, and by design. Refer to page 14 of the Trip 
Optimizer Supplemental Operator Training job aid for more information. ABTH Section 7, Item 
7.2 does not apply to Operation in Enhanced Auto Independent mode.   
 
When Trip Optimizer transitions from Auto Control to Manual Control the system will always 
return to Manual Control with the fence up – this is the system design for Trip Optimizer, 
regardless of railway company. This understanding was an essential compone nt of the briefing 
you should have received when you obtained your copy of the above job aid. This permits our 
trained and qualified Locomotive Engineers to manipulate the controls as may be required.    
 
If excessive slack action is encountered over the road, report it to PTC/FTO help Desk and give 
detailed MP location. Provide as much pinpoint information as possible. This enables the 
responsible CPKC team to validate the performance of our Energy Management  vendor and 
request future corrections to the system. CPKC’s professional Locomotive Engineers are the 
key to validating and improving this process. 
 
End of Train Device Mounting Procedure - EOT  
Recent End of Train Device failure drill downs have identified incorrect mounting as an ongoing issue. 
Employees are required to inspect the End of Train Device (EOT) before and after application, 
following the procedures outlined below.   
 
If you have any questions about these requirements contact your local manager for assistance.  
 
Points of Inspection:   
• EOT Housing undamaged, number legible, and appearing watertight  
• EOT Photocell and Light operational  
• EOT Hose and Glad Hand in good condition, free of damage, Glad Hand lock and  
locking spring present and functional   
• EOT Mounting Jaw and J-Hook secure to housing and functional  
• Hose Support applied to EOT glad hand  
• When possible EOT’s waiting for trains must be plugged in and charging
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-27 
 SYSTEM LOCOMOTIVE TECHNICAL INFO 
 APRIL 4, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 3 of 6 
 
 Mounting Procedure:   
1. Ensure end of car hose is in good condition as per AAR Rule 5. End hose and Glad Hand free of 
cuts, kinks, or damage.    
2. Always replace Glad Hand Gasket before applying EOT.  
3. Apply EOT by ensuring mounting jaw is square to the coupler and the J hook engages fully with the 
coupler. Tighten firmly (do not overtighten) apply the mounting jaw latch assembly to the handle to lock 
handle in place.   
4. Carefully align EOT and Car glad hands and couple together ensuring they seat fully.  
5. Once applied, ensure EOT is secure to coupler with no twists or kinks in car end hose or EOT hose 
with no foreign objects hanging lower than glad-hands.  
 6. Attach the EOT hose support to the locking handle of the EOT. Adjust the hose support to ensure 
the glad hands are a MINIMUM OF 5" from Top of Rail.  
7. Slowly open angle cock of car then inspect for leaks once air is applied. Repair or re -seat glad-
hands as needed. 
 
 
Handheld Air Gauges (Updated 1/1/2023)  
Handheld air gauges need to be verified as accurate to within +/- 3 psi. Accuracy can be verified by 
connecting the handheld air gauge to the brake pipe air hose of a locomotive and comparing the 
pressure against the locomotive brake pipe gauge. If the pressure displayed on the handheld gauge 
exceeds tolerance it must not be used. Employees using handheld air gauges should verify accuracy at 
least once annually.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-27 
 SYSTEM LOCOMOTIVE TECHNICAL INFO 
 APRIL 4, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 4 of 6 
 
FTO Requirements  
To maximize fuel savings, crews are required to use Fuel Trip Optimizer (when so equipped) on 
all trains.   
 
In the event the timetable speed is higher than the Fuel Trip Optimizer system will allow, and all 
other  exception reporting contact the Operations Support Desk (PTC/FTO Desk):  
 
To ensure a quicker response from the Operations Support Desk, please have the following 
information ready: 
1. Train ID and totals 
2. Initial and final terminals 
3. A clear description of the issue 
 
Your continued use of energy management systems helps reduce  carbon emission and fuel 
consumption, contributing to significant cost savings. 
 
Exceptions noted must be promptly reported to your respective Road Foreman and PTC/FTO 
help desk.  
 
Enhanced Distributed Power Software  
CP is installing several software upgrades for Distributed Power (DP) equipped locomotives to expand 
DP functionality and improve the operation. These features include:  
• Removal of Transition Penalties – No penalty brake application when transitioning into or out 
of DP  
• Enhanced Setout Mode – Remote will maintain a brake application once set out providing 
roll-away protection  
• Incremental Linking/Unlinking - Incrementally link or unlink locomotives without ending DP  
• Remote Same/Opposite Selection and Display – During DP setup remote orientation will 
default to "Unknown", forcing operator to select "Same or Opposite" to complete linking.  In 
addition, the remote orientation will be displayed on the lead locomotive DP operation screen.  
• Automatic Remote Status Repeating – Mid-train remote(s) will repeat status messages back 
to the lead locomotive, reducing communication losses  
• Manual Radio Test – Enables an operator to test the DP radios to aid with troubleshooting 
communication issues  
• Limited Penalty – A lead locomotive-initiated penalty will result in an equalizing reservoir and 
brake pipe reduction to approximately 58 psi. 
• Link Select-ability – Allows CP to link to more foreign locomotives. (CN, CSX, FXE,  
KCS, NS)  
All features may not be available or may have limited functionality, depending on how many 
locomotives in your train are equipped with the new software. Installation of the software  upgrade will 
take place over the next few months.  Required changes to the General Operating  Instructions (GOI) 
will be issued through system bulletins.  There will also be DP feature job aids produced and 
distributed over the coming weeks.  
 
New form Utilized by Mechanical – Schedule B Consist Information Form 582-3  
Locomotive Mechanical will be utilizing a new form indicating completion of Locomotive brake test, 
completion of daily inspection, lead and remote consist status, defective equipment, and set up 
information/guidelines. This form can be utilized at repair facilities, as well as field locations.  
Upon taking charge of consist with a Schedule B Consist information form, transfer the pertinent 
information to the Q-8065 Crew Information form.  
Part 1 – sign off that the locomotive brake test has been completed, including date, time, location and 
person certifying completion.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-27 
 SYSTEM LOCOMOTIVE TECHNICAL INFO 
 APRIL 4, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 5 of 6 
 
Part 2 – sign off on locomotive daily inspection date, time, location, and person certifying completion.  
Part 3 – will list locomotives in lead consist, run status, Dynamic Brake status (disabled, inoperative, 
cut-out, operational, if cut in and the factor).  This will also indicate the remote consist.  
Part 4 – will indicate defective locomotives safe to travel, movement restrictions and person certifying 
movement.  
Part 5 – dynamic brake set-up instructions/factors. 
 
 Securement of Brake Handles/Seats on Locomotives  
Several incidents have occurred where trains have accidentally been placed into emergency due to the 
locomotive engineer’s seat on EVO locomotives swiveling around and contacting the automatic brake 
handle on the 105 style control stand.   
Locomotive engineers are reminded that when setting up these locomotives for trail/remote operation, 
the automatic brake handle must be secured using the pin provided (when equipped). In addition,  
locomotives equipped with the newer "SEATS INC" style of seat, must be locked in the forward position 
using the locking mechanism when trailing or used as a remote. 
 
 
 
Distributed Power Radio Circuit Breaker  
In the past there was an issue regarding interpretation of the Distributed Power Radio circuit breaker. 
On the CP 11 fleet (CP8900-CP8960), the Distributed Power Radio circuit breaker is located on the 
Engine Control (EC) panel labeled as "DISTRIBUTED POWER". Cycling of this circuit breaker will not 
un-link the distributed power system when performing a flow sensor check.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-27 
 SYSTEM LOCOMOTIVE TECHNICAL INFO 
 APRIL 4, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 6 of 6 
 
 
 
 
Locking the Rear Door – GE Locomotives  
When required to lock all doors of the controlling locomotive per Section 4 of GOI, note that the rear 
door on the engineers’ side has a sliding tab, pictured below. This must be positioned to deploy the 
deadbolt and can require some additional pressure on the door and/or jiggling the slider to ensure the 
deadbolt extend. Also, note that when the deadbolt is correctly deployed, the door handle is also 
locked and will no longer rotate.  
 
Ensure that the deadbolt is fully deployed to properly secure the rear door, before locking the front door 
and leaving the controlling locomotive unattended.  
 
Note: The engineer’s rear door can be locked from the outside on AC4400’s (CP1 -10 & CEFX), 
however, on EVO’s (CP11-12) they must be locked from the interior per the sliding bolt process 
described above.  
 
If you are unable to lock a locomotive for any reason notify the dispatcher. Crews are required to 
secure required keys from local Road Foreman or Manager. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Jeffrey McInnis – Asst. Director Operating Practices & Rules - US

GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 1 of 24 
 
General Order A-4 dated January 1, 2025 is cancelled. 
Current "A" General Orders in Effect: 1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 19, 20, 23, 24, 27, 29 & 30. 
 
Change in this General Order: PTC Log In for Southern Region Effective May 2, 2025 @ 22:45 
 (Pgs. 1, 2, 3 & 4). 
 
This bulletin is structured as follows:  
A. Safety Alerts – Urgent notices.  
B. Software Updates – will display information relevant to software updates from the minimum 
deployable version forward.  
C. Operating Instructions – will display instructions related to proper operation of PTC. 
A. PTC SAFETY ALERTS  
None.  
 B. SOFTWARE UPDATES 
 
Consist Information  
• Crews must verify lead locomotive in consist.  
• Crews must accurately input consist information. When the consist is changed, crews must update 
consist information in the system prior to departing that location.   
• When inputting train length, the actual train length will be used. Train Length including the 3% is not 
to be used.  
• If confirmation that any of the above information is not correct, inform the train dispatcher and be 
governed by their instructions. 
 
PTC Automatic Consist   
PTC Automatic Consist population is now functional once a train has initialized any subsequent 
changes to the consist must be manually adjusted.  
Some trains may not receive automatic consist for various reasons.  This function does not relieve the 
crew of ensuring consist accuracy. 
 
 
##PTC Log in for US Southern Region Employees with new Employee ID 
Effective on 02-May-2025 @ 2245, crews logging into PTC will be required to use their new 
employee ID and PIN as described in the ePins One Pager document.  Crews that are currently 
logged into PTC and operating in an ACTIVE, DISENGAGED, or RESTRICTED state are not 
required to re-login to the PTC system.  If there is a situation where the crew goes to the CUT -
OUT state after the effective time of this General Order, they will be required to perform a crew 
logout and re-initialize the system and use their new employee ID and PIN as described in the 
ePins One Pager document.  If there are any issues, please contact the PTC help desk. 
 
 ePins Quick Reference Guide for Southern Region -Continued on next page

PTC Error and Malfunction Notification WEG-SAF-11352 (#2006) 
Due to an identified PTC malfunction, If an incorrect direction of travel has been selected during 
initialization of PTC crews are instructed to:  
1) Enter Restricted mode 
2) Exit Restricted mode 
3) Select the correct direction of travel to get back to Active 
 
Shoving Move Restrictions  
When completing a shove move past a permissive signal PTC will now restrict trains to a maximum 
speed of 20 mph for freight and 30 mph for passenger trains.

" Sync" error  
If a "Sync" flag appears on the PTC onboard screen, it is a result of the onboard information  
not in synchronization with the Back Office System information.  After acknowledgement of  
synchronization error, trains must immediately reduce to restricted speed.  Trains may return to 
maximum authorized speed once the onboard is back in ACTIVE state.   
 
In cases of rolling track file changes, crew will be notified by track bulletin that a PTC track file change 
will be occurring and if a sync error occurs during these advertised times, crews will need to reselect 
their track location and confirm track selection and the system will return ACTIVE. This can be 
completed at track speed. If the system does not recover reduce to restricted speed and contact the 
PTC help desk.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL

A rolling PTC track file change allows for a track file change while active PTC trains are on the  
subdivision.

Onboard Functionality for Train Movements with Inoperable PTC System  
In order to assist compliance with regulatory speed restrictions, crews will encounter the below screens 
when transitioning from Active to a degraded state at speed. Stopped trains will not see this 
functionality.   
During an unintended PTC state change, crews must reduce speed within 2 minutes to comply with the 
below speeds for freight and passenger trains to avoid PTC enforcement.    
Once train speed is reduced, crews can acknowledge the normal degraded state prompt.  
o All freight trains must reduce to at least 49 MPH (see current PTC Rules "A" General Order  
referencing GCOR 18.12 for applicable speed)  
o All passenger trains must reduce to at least 59 MPH (see current PTC Rules "A" General  
Order referencing GCOR 18.12 for applicable speed)  
o Degraded State acknowledgement prompt will not be available until travelling under the  
required track speed.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS

Location Menu  
1. The location menu is now accessible at any speed.  
• Below for reference only. 
 
2. The existing screen for selecting the locomotive track location is updated to distinguish it from the 
prompt to select the track location of the leading edge of the train.  
• The location prompt "SELECT CURRENT CONTROLLING LOCOMOTIVE TRACK"
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 16 of 24 
 
Exclusion Zone  
An exclusion zone is a portion of the train’s calculated route that the on-board segment cannot 
determine matches the train’s actual route due to a switch with unknown or unmonitored status.  The 
on-board segment does not enforce or prompt for any target within an exclusion zone.  This means 
trains will transition to ACTIVE state faster and more often.      
 
Below are conditions where on-board shall generate an exclusion zone:  
1. State is ACTIVE  
Orientation is forward.  
A switch with unknown or unmonitored status.  
 
2. State is DISENGAGED  
Orientation is forward.  
A switch with unknown or unmonitored status. 
Example 1 – Active state with Exclusion Zone where the track is colored grey 
 
Map not available  
Updated reason codes to be displayed under the "Map not available" banner.  
New reason code "waiting for switch and signal status":  
• Reason for the delay:  
o Allows time to accept wayside communication for the route of the train.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL

Train exits PTC track  
Updated the prompts to be displayed when the train approaches and exits PTC track.  
All of the prompts for exiting PTC track are only displayed while the locomotive is moving:

 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL

Flags  
Addition of a "HORN" flag to make the crew aware of faults that may prevent the on -board  
segment from automatically sounding the train horn at a grade crossing.  
1. Added a yellow "HORN" flag  
2. Shortened the "NON COMM" flag to "COMM"  
3. Shifted the position of several flags.  
4. Shortened the "NO CAB" flag to "CAB". This is for information only, CP doesn’t use Cab  
Signals.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 19 of 24 
 
Acknowledge Continued Movement in Restricted State  
New prompts when the on-board is in restricted state.  The crew will need to periodically acknowledge 
while in RESTRICTED state otherwise the on-board will initiate braking.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 20 of 24 
 
Grade Crossing Malfunction 
 
 
When dual initializing with foreign railroads and operating with active PTC  
You may receive a prompt for BULLETIN VOID. This is to acknowledge a current bulletin has been 
voided. The new feature is being used in relation with the foreign railroad software updates. Canadian 
Pacific IS NOT using this feature. You will need to acknowledge prompt.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 21 of 24 
 
Positive Train Control Onboard Components  
PTC onboard components are safety devices.  Unless otherwise authorized, on subdivisions in  
which PTC has not been implemented, crews are prohibited from:  
• Cutting out PTC Train Control Cutout breakers (Figure 1 – Train Control Cutout  
Breakers)  
• Performing functions on the onboard computer display (Figure 2 – Computer Display  
Unit), or  
• Tampering with any aspect of the locomotive PTC system.  
 
Figure 1: PTC Train Control Cutout Breakers Figure 2: Computer Display Unit (CDU)  
 
Note that PTC system captures all PTC activity and will record and report failure to comply with these 
requirements.  
 
PTC Cut Out  
Removing green "PTC CUT OUT" tag prior to Initializing:  
This tag is for PTC cut out in Canada only per Bulletin B-L040-19, to eliminate faulty undesired brake 
applications in non-PTC territory. 
 
The bottom of the tag reads, "THIS TAG TO BE REMOVED IF LOCOMOTIVE REQUIRED FOR PTC". 
At any point in US PTC territory, remove the tag and cut in the toggle switches for an Active PTC 
working locomotive. Then proceed with the initializing process before you depart.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 22 of 24 
 
Initializing PTC  
When operating within PTC designated track segments, with PTC equipped lead locomotive, the 
engineer must initialize the PTC system under these conditions:  
• prior to entering PTC track segments or ready to receive track authority.  
• when a PTC-equipped locomotive is placed in the lead position.  
• when relieving a PTC train; or  
• when instructed by the train dispatcher.  
 
When initializing the reverser must be in the direction of travel. If initialization fails,  
contact train dispatcher and be governed by their instructions. The entire train must be on PTC  
entry track or PTC enabled Main track not over any switches or within 100 feet of signals prior  
to going active.  
 
If crew is presented with the banner ‘NEW SOFTWARE AVAILABLE’ the crew must:  
• Select ‘No’  
• Attempt to initialize  
• If unsuccessful, report issues to the PTC help desk 
 
CDU display will look like this:
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 23 of 24 
 
Departure Test (Updated 1/1/2023)  
A departure test must be performed:   
• When prompted by the system  
o The PTC system will prompt a new test every 96 hours  
• At the trains initial station, prior to operating on PTC territory  
• When taking charge of a train without direct transfer or verbal communication with the  
previous crew 
o Departure test information recorded on the Crew Information Form is considered a  
direct transfer  
• Anytime the PTC breakers have been cycled off/on  
 
 When attached to equipment, the following steps must be followed when required to perform a  
departure test or turn the PTC breakers off or on:  
• If locomotive or train air brakes will not prevent movement of the attached train, secure the  
train per securement rules  
• Place remote locomotive consists in distributed power trains in set out mode prior to  
performing the departure test  
• Fully apply the independent brake  
• Close the angle cock on the rear locomotive of the lead consist  
• Release the automatic brake  
• Turn on/off PTC circuit breakers (when authorized) or perform PTC initialization and  
departure test  
• Where practical, perform the departure test or cycling of PTC breakers prior to coupling to  
equipment  
• When conducting a departure test, the generator field switch must be in the On position  
• Once the PTC system shuts down or initialization and departure test is complete, recover  
the air on the locomotive consist and open the angle cock on the rear locomotive of the  
lead locomotive consist 
 
Selecting Track  
The reverser must be in the direction of travel prior to making a PTC track selection. Do not select your 
location if train is within 100’ of a switch or Control Point. 
 
PTC On Screen Soft Cut Out/Restricted Mode  
Soft Cut Out  
Except as otherwise instructed, a soft cut out of the PTC system may only be used when:  
• more than 5 percent of the cars in any train operating PTC have inoperative brakes  
• helper locomotives are being used as the lead engine  
Restricted Mode  
Restricted mode must be used for the following activities.  
Restricted mode must be exited immediately when completed with activities.   
o Setouts  
o Switching enroute  
o When changing reverser direction  
o When required to clear in order to meet on account of train length  
o To reduce walking distance to a crossing at grade in order to provide warning as required by PTC 
onboard for a bulletined crossing  
o When loading/unloading of work trains under direction of MW Employee in Charge  
o Track out of service  
Prior to coming out of Restricted Mode, the reverser must be in the direction of travel.  
When entering the Main Track for head room PTC must be active. It is prohibited to travel between 
stations leaving PTC in restricted mode.
GENERAL ORDER NO. A-30 
 SYSTEM PTC OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS 
 APRIL 15, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 24 of 24 
 
 
PTC Hard Cut Out-Operating PTC Breakers or Toggle switches  
Crews are prohibited from cutting out the PTC system and turning off PTC breakers unless  authorized 
to do so. Any unauthorized use of the PTC Breakers or PTC toggle switches will be considered a 
violation of current rules for Altering Equipment.  The PTC Helpdesk must be contacted and document 
the operation or cut out of any PTC breakers and/or switches. Only cutout PTC switches or breakers 
when instructed by VP or designee. Report any PTC switches or breakers cut out or found to be cutout 
to Mechanical and the PTC Helpdesk as soon as possible. 
 
Wayside Signals Unusual Conditions at other than Automatic Interlockings   
When information displayed by PTC and aspect of the wayside signal system do not correspond, the 
engineer must operate according to the most restrictive information presented by PTC or the signal 
system.  
If a permissive indication is visually confirmed in the field, the crew must press the prompt (soft key) 
indicating authority has been received in order to remove the red fence and proceed.   
If a permissive indication is not provided in the field, the crew must:  
(a) comply with the requirements of GCOR 9.12.3; and press the button indicating authority has been 
received in order to remove the red fence and proceed.   
 
Trip Completion  
At the end of each PTC trip, the locomotive engineer must:  
• log off the system using the crew log off key; you must also press the Accept Key to  
acknowledge the degraded system state.  
• complete a trip report and submit it with all applicable portions completed to PTC Trip  
Reports and placed in a location designated per Notice.  
 
Trip reports are available on the FIT. Job aids and functionality reference material can be obtained by 
contacting your local supervisor or designee outlined per Notice. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Jeffrey McInnis – Asst. Director Operating Practices & Rules - US

US RULEBOOK for ENGINEERING EMPLOYEES

a Lookout and Item C Lookout Signals to Warn Employees are changed to read as

B. Duties of a Lookout  
While performing the duties of a Lookout they must:  
• Devote their entire attention to detecting approaching trains or on track 
equipment and give warning to Roadway Workers.  
• Not be assigned other duties while functioning as a Lookout.  
• Remain at their position until the Roadway Worker in Charge determines that 
the warning is no longer necessary, or they are relieved by another Lookout.  
• Not foul tracks unless necessary in the performance of their duties. If it’s 
necessary to foul a track to perform his lookout duties, it should be discussed in 
the job briefing as well as the location of where the watchman/lookout will 
position himself.  
• Have the appropriate equipment to perform their duties. The appropriate 
equipment is defined as the capability to warn employees through the use of an 
audible (whistle/horn) and visual device which could be a white disc, white light 
or just pointing with your arm in the direction, when required.  
 
C. Lookout Signals to Warn Employees  
Give signal to warn employees of an approaching train or on track equipment as 
follows:  
When using a white disc or white light: 
• Sound a warning whistle or horn.  
• Hold the white disc at arm’s length above head.  
• Then hold white disc horizontally at arm's length, toward the place designated 
in the Job Briefing where employees are to go to clear the tracks.  
 
When using your arm to point: 
• Sound a warning whistle or horn.  
• Extend your arm above your head.  
• Then point your arm toward the place designated in the Job Briefing where 
employees are to go to clear the tracks.  
  
Give signal to employees when it is safe to resume work as follows:  
• Hold the white disc horizontally at arm's length or extend your arm pointing 
toward the work site.  
 
NOTE: A Lookout assigned to protect only one employee who is performing work where 
advance Lookout(s) are not required does not need to be equipped with a visual warning 
device if they are within 25 feet of that individual, but the audible warning device i s still 
required. When working as a Lookout and you are right next to the roadway worker, such 
as a welder, a tap on the shoulder may also be used to get their attention for them to go 
to the place of safety.

Change in this General Order: Effective 00:01 May 3, 2025 the System Special Instructions Section 6 
Dimensional Equipment will be replaced in its entirety and replaced with the following. 
 
 
 
Starting April 30th, Dimensional Protection Notices will be issued through the Dimensional 
Clearance Application alongside Dimensional Clearance Messages from the KCS clearance 
office. Access the application here: https://dimensionalclearance.cpr.ca/  
 
Please note that DPNs issued by CPR_Clearances@CPKCR.com will only take effect following 
DayN integration, replacing KCS-issued notices. 
 
During the DayN transition period, trains handling Dimensional Traffic may continue operating 
under existing Dimensional authority.

CPKC System Special Instructions No.1, Section 6 Dimensional Equipment, is changed to read 
in its entirety as follows: 
 
Section 6 - Dimensional Equipment 
 
1.0 General  
Wherever the term "train" appears herein, it also applies to engines and transfers.  Wherever the term 
"protection notice" appears herein, it also applies to "blanket clearance."  
 
1.1 Dimensional Shipment Standards  
A dimensional shipment is one, which exceeds the maximum standards of size, weight, and/or height of 
center of gravity as established by CPKC.  
 
CPKC defines dimensional traffic as being any shipment exceeding Plate F.  
 
 
 
Dimensional traffic may be easily identified by width, height, and length.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-36 
 SSI SECTION 6 – DIMENSIONAL EQUIPMENT 
 APRIL 29, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 3 of 13 
 
 
2.0 Protection Notices  
A protection notice affords protection only upon Main Tracks, Sidings, Interchange Tracks, or other tracks 
specifically identified in the protection notice.  
 
2.1   Format of Protection Notices  
The format of the protection notice has been divided into 6 sections: 
 
"Section 1":  Lists e-mail addresses which receive a copy.  Specifies the file number, the classification, 
and indicates if the shipment is governed by Specific Restrictions.  
• A file number commencing with "DL" indicates that General Restrictions apply (e.g., 
DL4011109).  
• A file number commencing with "RL" indicates General and Specific Restrictions apply 
(e.g., RL4013099).  
 
"Section 2": Specifies the date the Protection Notice was issued. Specifies the characteristics of the 
shipment, including the car number(s), car marshaling, type of lading, shipper/origin, 
consignee/destination, full route, and CPKC routing.  
 
"Section 3":  Specifies the measurements of the shipment:  height, width, length, gross weight, center 
of gravity from the truck center and the combined center of gravity.  
 
"Section 4":  Specifies the subdivision name and the mileage points between which the protection notice 
applies on the subdivision. Specifies the W-code Classification.  
 
"Section 5":   Specifies the "Specific Restrictions" that apply to a load at precise locations along its 
routing.  They are listed by mileage in the sequence in which they will be encountered.  Some examples 
are  reduce speed over bridges or passing specific obstructio ns; stop, examine, and proceed with crew 
observing the movement; and special marshaling.  
 
"Section 6":  Specifies the "Code 6 Instruction message" and file number of the Protection Notice.  The 
"Code 6 Instruction message" on the train consist must be exactly as shown in Section 6 of the Protection 
Notice.  
 
2.2 Dimensional Traffic – Protection Notice Exceptions  
All dimensional traffic, with the following exceptions, must be protected by a protection notice:  
 
Piggyback flat cars  loaded with truck trailers not exceeding 17’ 6" ATR (Above Top of Rail) by 8’ 6" 
wide.  This traffic can be handled without restriction.  
 
Fully enclosed (roof, sides and ends) multilevel traffic, not exceeding 19’ 1" ATR (Above Top of Rail). 
This traffic can be handled without restriction between the locations shown below.  
 
Double stack container traffic, not exceeding 20’ 4" ATR (Above Top of Rail), equivalent to two  
(2) 9’ 6" high, by 8’ 6" wide containers stacked (double stack cars identified on train consist as plate "H" 
or "I", either empty or loaded with containers single tier are considered non-dimensional).  
Note: This item covers containers loaded double stacked in:  CONVENTIONAL CARS EQUIPPED FOR 
DOUBLE STACK OPERATION AND MULTI-PLATFORM CARS.

Locations NOT identified in 2.2 will require a protection notice for the movement of the 
equipment described.  
 
2.3   Overloaded cars   
Unless otherwise indicated on train consist, overloaded cars may be accepted without additional 
authority. Overloaded cars which are NOT acceptable for movement without additional protection, will be 
identified as such on train consists and must be authorized by dimensional protection notice. 
 
2.4 Copy of Protection Notice  
A copy of the Protection Notice must:  
• accompany the movement from origin station to destination station,  
• be attached to the shipment’s waybill (if a waybill is provided).  
 
2.5 Information on Protection Notice  
The following information will be provided immediately after the addresses on each Protection Notice.  
Examples:  
• DL4011109 W-08 GENERAL RESTRICTIONS APPLY  
or  
• RL4013099 W-05-07 GENERAL AND SPECIFIC RESTRICTIONS APPLY  
a) File Number  
• A file number commencing with "DL" indicates that General Restrictions apply. (e.g. 
DL4011109)  
• A file number commencing with "RL" indicates General and Specific Restrictions apply. (e.g. 
RL4013099)  
b) Classification  
• W-08 indicates the classification of the shipment.  
• W-05-07 indicates the smallest and largest classification when the classification varies 
throughout the shipments entire route.  
c) Restrictions  
• "General Restrictions Apply," indicates that subsection 4.0 applies.  
• "General and Specific Restrictions Apply," indicates that SPECIFIC RESTRICTIONS of the 
protection notice also apply.  
 
2.6 The crew of a train or engine handling dimensional traffic  
Must comply with all applicable specific restrictions listed in the Protection Notice and are responsible to 
ensure dimensional traffic is not diverted from the limits stated in section 4 of the Protection Notice.  If 
necessary to move the shipment outside of these limits, a revised protection notice must be obtained.  
 
In terminals where crews are not in possession of Protection Notices, the person in charge is responsible 
to protect these limits. 
 
2.7   Diverting Dimensional Traffic from Limits under Section 4   
The crew of a train or engine handling dimensional traffic is responsible to ensure a dimensional shipment 
is not diverted from the limits stated in section 4 of the Protection Notice. If necessary to move the 
shipment in an area outside of these limits, a  revised protection notice must be obtained. In terminals 
where crews are not in possession of Protection Notices, the yardmaster is responsible to protect these 
limits.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-36 
 SSI SECTION 6 – DIMENSIONAL EQUIPMENT 
 APRIL 29, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 6 of 13 
 
3.0 Classification 
 
3.1 Classifying Dimensional Traffic   
Dimensional traffic is classified according to width, based on shipment being loaded on a car less than 
42 feet. This information will be included on the train consist in a "Code 6 Instruction Message."  
 
Classification Effective Width 
W-00 10’ 8" or Less 
W-01 10’ 9" to 11’ 0" 
W-02 11’ 1" to 11’ 6" 
W-03 11’ 7" to 12’ 0" 
W-04 12’ 1" to 12’ 6" 
W-05 12’ 7" to 13’ 0" 
W-06 13’ 1" to 13’ 6" 
W-07 13’ 7" to 14’ 0" 
W-08 14’ 1" to 14’ 6" 
W-09 14’ 7" to 15’ 0" 
W-10 15’ 1" and over 
 
For overhanging shipments or shipments loaded on cars of 42 feet or longer, the "Effective Width" is 
reflected by a more restrictive classification.   
 
Note: Classification W-00 refers to dimensional traffic that has an effective width of 10’8" or less (e.g. 
shipment exceeds CP maximum weight or height standards but not maximum width standards).  
 
In the application of 4.2 (meet and passing), non-dimensional traffic shall be treated as being W-00. 
 
4.0 General Restrictions 
The following definitions apply in this subsection:  
 
Restricted Meet: When the train handling the wide traffic is required to move past trains, equipment, or 
other permissible wide traffic, movements must be stopped, and inspection made to ensure that adequate 
clearance exists before proceeding.  
Note:  A Restricted Meet is not required at the following location(s) where tracks are known to diverge 
onto separate roadbeds. 
 
Subdivision Location 
Watertown Between MP 95.36 at Juneau BLVD and MP 
99.43 N. Brookfield RD NO 1 and NO 2 MT’s. 
 
Unrestricted Meet: Movements may meet or pass without restrictions.   
 
The meet and pass instructions listed herein are calculated on standard track centers between adjacent 
tracks on the same roadbed. Standard track centers are 13 feet between main tracks and 14 feet between 
a main track and a track other than a main track.  Some locations on CP have track centers that exceed 
these standards. At such locations where track centers between adjacent tracks on the same roadbed 
are known to exceed these standards, meet and pass instructions may be relaxed if a Restricted Meet 
takes place. 
 
4.1 Specific Meet/Pass Instructions  
Classification W-09 & W-10:   
• Due to extreme width, shipment to be moved in DAYLIGHT ONLY, unless otherwise authorized by 
the Superintendent – Field Operations.  
 
Trains handling W-09 or W-10 traffic must approach all track units prepared to stop unless it is determined 
that adequate clearance exists.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-36 
 SSI SECTION 6 – DIMENSIONAL EQUIPMENT 
 APRIL 29, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 7 of 13 
 
Classification W-08 to W-10:    
Adjacent Main Tracks (Multiple main track Territory)  
• All adjacent main tracks to be kept clear of trains and equipment during movement.  
• Also: See item 4.3 for further restrictions applicable at SPECIFIC MILEAGES or SIDINGS where 
track centers are LESS than standard.  
 
4.2 Meet/Pass Instruction Charts  
These charts do not apply on the Northeast US East Region. See item 4.4.  
 
The Meet/Pass Instruction Charts 1 and 2 may be used to determine meet and pass restrictions.   
 
Some locations exist where track centers do not meet standard, refer to item 4.3 for exception locations

5.0 Handling Procedures 
 
5.1 Permission in Train   
Before any dimensional traffic may be placed in a train, permission of the Chief of Train Dispatchers 
(COTD) must be secured.   
 
The conductor must confirm with Train Dispatcher/Operations Supervisor that authority has been granted 
for movement of a dimensional traffic before leaving their initial terminal or when picking up dimensional 
traffic enroute.  
 
Note: Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor will be responsible for notifying adjoining Train 
Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor territories for that train movement.  
 
Note: Permission will be withheld until appropriate NEXUS dimensional information has been updated.  
 
When requesting permission from the Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor, the employee doing 
so must supply the following information:  
• Car initials and number,  
• Classification (such as W-03, or W-03-07),  
• Specific Restrictions, if any,  
• Protection Notice file number,  
• Any other information that may be required.  
 
5.2 Setting out Dimensional Traffic  
Before setting out dimensional traffic (W -01 or greater), at locations where yardmasters cannot provide 
the necessary protection against other movement, the crew must obtain permission from the Train 
Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor. The conductor will notify the Train Dispatcher or Operations 
Supervisor the car initial and number and location of dimensional shipment. The Train Dispatcher or 
Operations Supervisor will then issue a track bulletin to approaching train movements if the car is set out 
on an adjacent track next to a main track or controlled siding advising the location of the dimensional 
shipment and any instructions pertaining to the protection of such shipment.  
 
5.3 Protection of Moves  
Where Yardmasters or other employees in charge of movements are on duty to instruct moves, the Train 
Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor will notify them of the presence of dimensional shipment in a train 
before that train enters the yard under their jurisdiction.  The Yardmaster or other employee in charge of 
movements within these yards will be responsible to keep crews informed of the location of conflicting 
dimensional traffic within those yards, while on duty.  Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor  will 
provide protection against main track movements as outlined in Item 5.3.  
 
5.4 Operating Through Yards, Sidings, Interchange Track and Within Yard Limits    
Crews must be especially watchful when operating through yards, sidings, interchange tracks and yard 
limits to ensure ample side clearance exists between dimensional traffic being handled and equipment 
on adjacent tracks.  
 
Crews must also ensure ample side clearance exists between equipment being handled and dimensional 
traffic on adjacent tracks.  
 
Where overhead or side clearance is doubtful, movement must be stopped, and inspection is made to 
ensure that adequate clearance exists before proceeding.  
 
5.5 Marshaling of Dimensional Shipments  
Unless otherwise indicated in the car marshaling instruction of the protection notice, dimensional 
shipments may be marshaled without restriction. However, to permit visual observation by the crews, the 
dimensional shipments requiring a physical examinatio n in order to clear a specific location, shall be 
marshaled as close as possible to the lead locomotive.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-36 
 SSI SECTION 6 – DIMENSIONAL EQUIPMENT 
 APRIL 29, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 13 of 13 
 
On trains operating without a manned caboose, all dimensional traffic that would normally be marshaled 
to permit visual observation by the crew shall be marshaled as close as possible to, but not more than 
2000 feet from the controlling unit.    
 
Note: Train consist, or protection notice will indicate dimensional shipments to which this item applies.  
 
5.6 Movement Past Other Traffic Adjacent Track  
When the dimensions of traffic do not permit unrestricted movement past other traffic on adjacent tracks 
and it is not practicable for the Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor to maintain blocking devices 
or to withhold operating authority, the Train Dispatcher or Operations Supervisor may use verbal 
instructions or issue a track bulletin to protect restricted meets against other main track movements.  
 
5.7 Joint Trackage   
Prior to a dimensional shipment being moved over joint trackage, permission must be obtain from the 
concerned railroad(s).  
 
5.8 Switching   
Dimensional shipments are not to be humped or kicked.

SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-38 
 ENGINEERING RULES PERTAINING TO EIC 
 JUNE 10, 2025

Page 1 of 3 
 
General Order A-8 dated January 1, 2025, is cancelled. 
Current "A" General Orders in Effect: 1, 7, 19, 23, 24, 27, 30, 31, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37 & 38. 
 
Change in this General Order: Safety upgrades to EIC. 
 
The EIC system allows foremen to electronically request and manage track protection. Based 
on input from EIC users, we are introducing safety upgrades in two phases . 
 
Phase 1: June 24, 2025 
• Reject Reason field: increase the length to 100 characters to include safety information.  
• GCOR Track Warrant: A new note and checkbox will be added to the "Report Clear Track 
Warrants" in GCOR territory, allowing users to confirm that all switches are properly lined and 
locked. 
• Enhanced Home Safe process: In GCOR territory, addition of enforced safety prompting (4 
second rule) to ensure correct portion of authority is cancelled during a Complete By. 
• Unsolicited Cancel: Revise the wording in the EIC dialog box to enhance clarity and ensure 
better user understanding. 
• Behind Train Fields:  Ability to insert a full train designation in Track & Time and Track 
Warrant including Psgr, Plow, and others.  
 
Phase 2: Sept 9, 2025 
• Current Subdivision Owner Display: For CROR and GCOR territories, you can now find the 
current subdivision owner. 
• Chicago & Winchester Subs:  New capability for double track EIC functionality. 
• Dispatcher/RTC approvals: Develop the Request/Acknowledgement/Feedback workflow 
within CROR and GCOR territories by incorporating Dispatcher/RTC approvals in the EIC 
Application. 
• Local Control Request: Develop new capabilities for local control requests at specific control 
points within a requested authority for CROR and GCOR territories.  
 
Quick reference guides and more details on the improvements will be provided closer to the 
implementation date(s). 
 
The following subdivisions are available for the use of EIC once the user has been through the 
rollout and deemed qualified for the use of EIC in the field: 
Portal, Carrington, Lignite, Newtown,  Noyes, Detroit Lakes, Veblen, Elbow Lake, Paynesville, St. Paul, 
Withrow, Merriam Park, River,  Tomah, M&P, Watertown, C&M Sub between the Cut Off and Rondout 
and including Shermer and Bryn Mawr to B-17, CTC portion of the Chicago Sub, Nitrin, Tracy, Waseca, 
Owatonna, Sheldon,  Jackson, Marquette, Davenport,  Ottumwa, Kansas City,   Moosehead, Bangor, 
Canadian, Canadian Connector, Freight and Colonie.  
 
Below you will find the rules that pertain to Engineering Employees receiving electronic track authorities. 
These rules are in  effect with this General Order and will be added into the upcoming CPKC US 
Rulebook for Engineering Employees. 
 
10.3 Track and Time – No change, as written in current manual. 
10.3.4 Track and Time Acknowledgment – Added last paragraph. 
14.2  Designated Limits – Added the word siding so it reads, siding switches. 
14.9 Copying Track Warrants – Added item C. Receiving Track Warrants using Railroad Supplied Electronic 
Device. 
21.1.2 Requesting OTS for Controlled Tracks – Added the words verbally or electronically. 
21.6 Foul Time – Second paragraph added.

10.3 Track and Time 
The control operator may authorize an employee to occupy a track or tracks within specified limits for a certain 
time period. Authority must include track designation, track limits, and either a time limit or the words "until 
released". The employee may use the track in either direction within the specified limits according to the track 
authority limits until the limits are verbally released. 
 
10.3.4 Track and Time Acknowledgment  
Track and time authority is transmitted verbally, it must be recorded and repeated to the control  
operator. Acknowledgment must be received before being acted upon.  
 
The control operator must maintain a record of the authority granted.   
 
When receiving track and time using a railroad supplied electronic device designed to request, receive, release 
or report clear of authority (e.g. Company Laptop) a viewable electronic form of the authority granted will be 
displayed by the device. Employees must use the electronic form to confirm authority limits. 
 
14.2  Designated Limits  
Track warrant limits must be designated by specifying track, where required, and specific locations such as 
siding switches, mile posts, or railroad identifiable points. However, station names may be used as follows: 
(Remaining portion of this rule unchanged). 
 
14.9 Copying Track Warrants  
The employee in charge must have a copy of the track warrant issued and must read and understand it. The 
copy must show the date. The following must occur when transmitted verbally:  
A.  Transmitting Track Warrants  
1. An employee will enter all of the information and instructions on the track warrant.  
2. The employee will repeat the preprinted and written information transmitted by the train dispatcher.  
3. The train dispatcher will check it and, if correct, will say "OK" and give the time and his initials.  
4. The employee will enter the "OK" time and the train dispatcher’s initials on the track warrant  
and repeat them to the train dispatcher.  
 
B.  In Effect  
1. The track warrant is not in effect until the "OK" time is shown on it.  
2. If the track warrant restricts movement or previously granted authority, it cannot be considered in effect 
by the train dispatcher until acknowledgment of the "OK" has been received.  
 
Employees may relay track warrant information from the Control Operator or Train Dispatcher.  
 
C. Receiving Track Warrants using Railroad Supplied Electronic Device  
When receiving a Track Warrant using a railroad supplied electronic device designed to request, receive, 
release or report clear of authority (e.g. Company Laptop) a viewable electronic form of the authority granted 
will be displayed by the device. Employees must use the electronic form to confirm authority limits. 
 
21.1.2 Requesting OTS for Controlled Tracks  
An employee requesting OTS for controlled track verbally or electronically, must inform the Train  
Dispatcher or Control Operator the limits and time needed and where the main track will be entered or  
fouled.  In addition, employees must ascertain if any track bulletin Form B or track bulletin removing a  
track from service are in effect within the territory that they will be fouling. Employees and equipment  
must not enter the main track at any other point, unless otherwise authorized.  
 
The Employee in Charge must make sure that the equipment or employees do not occupy or foul the  
track until OTS is provided. 
 
21.6 Foul Time  
Foul Time for Engineering Services will be considered exclusive track occupancy and employee receiving 
will copy and repeat the information received, when given verbally, back to the Train Dispatcher or Control 
Operator before it becomes effective.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-38 
 ENGINEERING RULES PERTAINING TO EIC 
 JUNE 10, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 3 of 3 
 
When receiving a Foul Time using a railroad supplied electronic device designed to request, receive, release 
or report clear of authority (e.g. Company Laptop) a viewable electronic form of the authority granted will be 
displayed by the device. Employees must use the electronic form to confirm authority limits.  
 
Before Train Dispatcher or Control Operator may grant foul time, all trains must be clear of that segment of 
track and other movements withheld once the foul time becomes effective.  
 
The Employee in Charge shall not permit the movement of trains or other on-track equipment into or  
within the working limits protected by Foul Time. Other employees may enter Foul Time once a Job  
Briefing is held with the Employee in Charge holding the Foul Time. The Working Limits form will be  
filled out accordingly.  Foul Time will not be made joint, and the working limits will be the specific  
segment of track granted on the Foul Time Form.  
 
Foul time is in effect until released by the requesting employee. 
 
23.3.5 Electronic Authority   
While it is in effect, all the contents of an authority electronically displayed shall be readily viewable by  
the Employee in Charge that is using the authority to provide OTS for a roadway work group.  
 
If the electronic display device malfunctions, fails, or cannot display an authority while it is in effect, the  
Employee in Charge shall either obtain a written or printed copy of the authority. On-track roadway  
maintenance machine and hi-rail movements must stop and establish another form of OTS without  
delay.   
 
In the event that a written or printed copy of the authority cannot be obtained or another form of OTS  
cannot be established after failure of an electronic display device, the Employee in Charge shall instruct all 
roadway workers to stop work and occupy a place of safety and conduct an OTS job briefing to determine 
the safe course of action with the roadway work group.

2.21 Electronic Devices 
This rule outlines the requirements for the use of electronic devices. Crew members are jointly responsible 
for compliance with the appropriate use of electronic devices. 
 
Electronic Device - An electronic or electrical device used to conduct oral, written, or visual communication; 
place or receive a telephone call; send or read an electronic mail message or text message; look at pictures; 
read a book or other written materi al; play a game; navigate the Internet; navigate the physical world; play, 
view, or listen to a video; play, view or listen to a television broadcast; play or listen to music; execute a 
computational function; or, perform any other function that is not nec essary for the health or safety of the 
person and that entails the risk of distracting the employee or another employee from a safety related task.  
 
The use of any electronic device is prohibited if that use would interfere with an employee’s performance of 
safety-related duties. 
 
Railroad Supplied Electronic Devices 
Railroad operating employees may use railroad supplied electronic devices to send or receive work related 
for authorized business purposes. Care and good judgement must always be used to ensure proper attention 
and concentration when performing any task. 
 
Railroad operating employees must not use a railroad supplied electronic device for purposes other than 
which it was intended or while: 
• Inside or outside the controlling cab of a locomotive, train or on -track equipment, unless there has 
been a safety briefing, and all crew members agree that it is safe to do so. 
• Operating the controls of a moving locomotive unless device is being used to reference a railroad 
rule, special instruction, timetable, track elevation chart or other directive and use does not interfere 
with any employee’s performance of safety related duties. 
• On the ground within 4 feet of any track. 
• On the ground and engaged in an active switching operation. 
• Riding rolling equipment during a switching operation. 
• At the controls of the locomotive and any other employee is assisting in the preparation of the train, 
engine(s), or on-track equipment, including testing of railroad equipment or brakes. 
 
Railroad authorized electronic devices may be used in the body of a business car or passenger train for 
railroad business when it will not interfere with an employee’s performance of safety related duties.
