General Security and will contain the following information: 
 
1.0  General Security  
1.1 Reporting Security Concern  
Train crews must immediately report to the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor, the CPKC Public 
Safety Communications Center (PSCC) or CPKC Railroad Police any security concern, security incident, 
criminal activity (known or suspected), suspicious activi ties, suspicious persons on or near Company 
property, and any other near miss or possible security threats.  They should also be alert for signs of 
theft, tampering or vandalism of critical safety devices.  
 
Note: More information on CPKC’s Security Plan and Programs can be found on CPKC Station.  
  
CPKC Public Safety Communications Center (PSCC) 
1–800–716–9132 
 
2.0  Security Alert Levels  
2.1   Alert Levels  
CPKC’s security program has 4 Alert Levels which incorporates all actions from the preceding levels:  
• Level 1 – Normal Day-to-Day Operations  
• Level 2 – Heightened Security Awareness  
• Level 3 – Credible Threat  
• Level 4 – Confirmed Threat  
If there is a reason to elevate CPKC’s Security Alert Level, the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor 
will receive specific information on actions to be taken.  Train crews will receive instructions by bulletin 
and/or from the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor.  
 
2.2  Alert Level 3  
At Alert Level 3, Alert Trains will be identified, and the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor notified  
of their status. The Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor must confirm the location of all Alert  
Trains in dark territory on a regular basis, at least every 60 minutes, and record this information.  
 
ALERT TRAINS are trains carrying certain dangerous Goods/Hazardous Materials.  The message "This 
is an Alert Train" will appear on the train consist in the header message area. Alternatively, you may be 
notified by the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor while en-route that your train is an Alert Train. 
 
2.3  Alert Level 3 Notification   
At Alert Level 3, train crews must notify the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor immediately of 
unusual or unexpected stops (e.g. red signals, defect detectors, undesired brake emergencies, etc.), 
BEFORE they exit the locomotive for any reason, includin g to inspect the train. While occupied, 
locomotive cab doors should be kept locked. 
   
3.0  Suspicious Objects   
3.1  Suspicious or Dangerous Objects   
Employees should be alert for any suspicious or dangerous objects on trains, tracks or CPKC property, 
including items which may be attached to or adjacent to tracks, switches, signals, or on the right-of-way.  
 
These objects can come in many different forms and may appear ordinary.  Examples of what to look 
for are:  
 • Unusual items, such as Improvised Explosive Devices (IED), on or attached to cars, 
especially placarded tank cars.  
• Apparent signs of tampering, sabotage, contraband or other unusual or prohibited items  
• Loaded cars with broken door seals and/or partially open doors  
• Hidden or abandoned bags, boxes or parcels,  
• Objects emitting an unusual sound, odor, mist, gas or vapor.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-43 
 SYSTEM SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS 
 SEPTEMBER 11, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 8 of 10 
 
 
3.2  Remote Monitoring Equipment  
Remote Monitoring Equipment (RME), such as GPS (Global Positioning System) devices are commonly 
being installed on highway trailers, railroad freight & tank cars and are not dangerous objects.  Per AAR 
Standard S-2045, they are:  
• Identified by a sticker, label or stencil:  
- At least 2" X 3"  
- In a highly visible bright yellow or orange with black lettering  
- Located within 12 inches of the sensor  
- With information describing the device indicating it's function and providing a phone     
number for information related to the device.   
They can also be located in various locations on rail cars and identified in UMLER if the RME is 
permanently mounted.  
 
3.3  Suspicious Object Is Found   
If a suspicious object is found:   
1. Do not attempt to move or touch it.  
2. Stay clear of the area and keep others clear of the area.  
3. If the object is a possible explosive:  
• do not use your radio or cellular phone to call for assistance unless you are at least 
300 feet away from the  object,   
• instruct all personnel to evacuate the area.  
4. Take note of any suspicious vehicles or people in the area  
5. Immediately notify the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor, your supervisor, or the PSCC  
 
3.4 Definitions:  
Improvised Explosive Device (IED) – is a device fabricated in an improvised manner incorporating 
explosives or destructive, lethal, noxious, pyrotechnic, or incendiary chemicals in its design. This device 
generally includes a power supply, a switch or time, and a detonator or initiator.  
 
Remote Monitoring Equipment (RME) applies to any device applied to a railcar or its lading that transmits 
a signal or records data that can be received by a remote receiver or retrieved at a later time by a carrier, 
shipper or other entity.  
 
4.0  Persons on CPKC Property  
Employees should report unknown persons on CPKC property to the PSCC.  
Note: Employees should not approach or confront unknown persons on or near CP property or railway 
tracks if they appear threatening, upset, depressed, or intoxicated. Reasonable efforts should be made 
to keep them under observation from a safe distance unt il CPKC or local police can respond.  Do not 
place yourself at risk. If you feel threatened back off and call 911 AND the PSCC.  
 
4.1 Remain Alert  
Remain alert for:  
• Individuals illegally riding in locomotives and on  trains.  
• Strangers or visitors on CPKC property. 
 
4.2 Visitors on Property  
If it is safe, approach strangers or visitors on the property and determine if they have a business need to 
be there. Check credentials and photo ID for individuals, including those identifying themselves as 
working for any government agency such as the Fe deral Railroad Administration (FRA), the 
Transportation Security Administration (TSA) or the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB).  All 
persons on CPKC property should have proper identification or be escorted by a CPKC employee.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-43 
 SYSTEM SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS 
 SEPTEMBER 11, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 9 of 10 
 
4.3  Report Suspicious Persons    
Immediately, report any suspicious or unauthorized people to the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor, 
your Supervisor or the PSCC who can arrange to have them escorted off the property.  Be prepared to 
provide details such as descriptions of the individual and/ or vehicles.  
 
5.0  Persons Riding Trains  
5.1 Report to Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor  
The conductor or other employee in charge must immediately report to the Train Dispatcher/Operation 
Supervisor whenever there are other persons riding in locomotives or other non -passenger rail 
equipment, excluding assigned crew members and supervisors performing their duties.  
 
5.2 Information to Report  
This report should identify the individual(s) name and what authorization they have for accompanying the 
train or equipment, including:  
• A company employee who is performing normal duties and has company ID   
• A company employee who possesses a signed access pass and has company ID  
• A non-employee who possesses a signed pass, a signed liability waiver form and a photo ID.  
 
5.3  Unauthorized Persons  
If there are unauthorized persons riding on the train, the train crew should:  
• Not proceed, OR stop at the next available location,   
            And  
• Notify the Train Dispatcher/Operation Supervisor or the PSCC  
 
6.0  Employee Identification   
Employee identification cards are issued to all CPKC employees. Employee identification cards include 
the employee’s name and employee number. The cards must be carried along with valid photo ID by all 
employees on duty, and both pieces of identification m ust be presented for on -demand checks by a 
company officer or by a customer while at a customer site. The employee identification cards are also 
used as access cards at designated facilities. Employee identification cards are nontransferable and the 
responsibility of each employee. If an employee’s card is incorrect, irreparably damaged, lost or stolen, 
the employee must contact their manager or nearest facilities section for replacement.   
 
7.0 Transportation Worker Identification Credentials (TWIC)  
Employees requiring unescorted access to secure areas of US marine ports are required to obtain and 
have in their possession a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) card.  Failure to obtain 
a TWIC will render an employee ineligible for ass ignments where TWIC cards are legally necessary for 
access to secure areas in the port.  
 
8.0  Disclosure of Sensitive Information   
8.1  Conversations Off Job or Workplace  
Be aware of personal conversations with others off the property concerning your job and workplace.  
Unusual interest in technical details should be reported to your supervisor or the PSCC.  
 
8.2  Request for Hazardous Material Information  
The heightened need for increased public security and for terrorist threat countermeasure planning by 
emergency responders has resulted in an increase in requests for information about our railway 
operations.  Much of the attention is focused on the transportation of hazardous materials. 
 
Anyone receiving a request for hazardous materials information or other suspicious questions regarding 
rail operations or critical infrastructures should ascertain as much detail as possible about the individual 
making the request, the organization he or she represents, and the intended use of any material that we 
might supply. Notify of all such requests to the PSCC and the Public Affairs Department for co-ordination 
of the appropriate response.
SYSTEM GENERAL ORDER NO. A-43 
 SYSTEM SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS 
 SEPTEMBER 11, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 10 of 10 
 
Exception: Requests from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) or the Federal Railroad 
Administration (FRA) for location and shipping information of hazardous materials shipments must be 
directed to the CPKC PSCC at 1-800-716-9132 for handling.  
 
NOTE: All CPKC employees are prohibited from providing any outside third party with information 
regarding hazardous materials movements, routing, volumes or storage.

Entire Sub CPKC Eastern Region Timetable NO 1, page 28, Remote Activated Switches and Remote 
activated Derail information is removed and replaced with the following information:   
Remote Activated Switches 
Radio Touch Tone power-controlled switches placed in service and are identified by signs 
for the On Station (OS) track segment reading BEGIN OS TRACK and END OS TRACK. 
Power Switches will be protected by switch point indicator signals. 
 
Shoreham  
• 1.0 BN University Switch. Green when lined for West runner and yellow when lined for 
Loop track. Crew member will transmit touch tone number #0101 for normal (West Runner) 
or #0102 for reverse (Loop Track) using radio channel (AAR 084-084).  Crew member can 
transmit touch tone number #0109 to query position of switch. 
 
• 1.5 Superior Connection/West Runner switch. Green (normal) when lined for west runner 
track and yellow (reverse) when lined for Superior Connection track.  Crew member will 
transmit touch tone number #0151 for normal (West Runner) or #0152 for reverse (Superior 
Connector) using radio channel (AAR 084 -084).  Crew member can transmit touch tone 
number #0159 to query position of switch. 
 
• 1.6 Superior Connector/BNSF transfer switch. Green (reverse) when lined for west runner 
and yellow (normal) when lined for BNSF transfer track. Crew member will transmit touch
GENERAL ORDER NO. C-15 
 PAYNESVILLE SUBDIVISION 
 MAY 13, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 3 of 4 
 
tone number #0161 for reverse (West Runner) or #0162 for normal (BNSF Transfer Track) 
using radio channel (AAR 084-084).  Crew member can transmit touch tone number #0169 
to query position of the switch. 
 
NOTE - The above two locations are incorporated together at the same location. The top 
signal indicator will be for Superior Connection/West Runner switch, while bottom signal 
indicator will be for Superior connector/BNSF transfer switch.  
 
The following will apply to the operation of the power -controlled switches by radio touch 
tone: 
• Train or engine movement must approach switch prepared to stop. 
• Use touch tone number for switch position before passing the OS sign location. This must 
be done for each movement over the switch. 
• Switch point indicator will change accordingly from green or yellow aspect based upon 
request. 
• Movement may proceed through the OS section once switch is lined and verified for route 
by switch point indicator. 
 
If indicator light displays Red, Flashing Red, White, or no indication is displayed, stop 
movement before passing OS sign. Switch must then be hand operated per GCOR 9.13.1 
(Hand Operation of Dual Control Switches), permission from control operator is not 
necessary to hand operate this switch.  
• Red – indicates occupancy of the switch 
• Flashing Red – indicates switch is out of correspondence (OOC) 
• White – Switch has been placed in Maintenance Mode 
 
Maintenance of Way movements must place switch in maintenance mode by use of MOW 
lock box on switch stand; then hand operate the switch as outlined above for their 
movements.   Maintenance of Way movements must be clear of switch location before 
deselecting MOW lockout box to return switch to power for remote operation.  
 
Remote Activated Derail 
Humboldt - Radio Touch Tone controlled Derail in service on Receiver 1 track at 
Humboldt MP 3.8. Derail will be protected by switch point indicator, Red for derailing 
position and Green for non-derailing position. 
 
The following will apply to the operation of the Radio Controlled Derail by radio touch 
tone: 
• Radio touch tone must be used before passing OS sign location 
• Crew member will transmit touch tone number #0381 using radio channel AAR (094 -
094) 
• The derail will then move to non-derailing position. 
• Derail indicator will change from red aspect to green aspect and will transmit message 
"3.8 HUMBOLDT DERAIL IS IN NON-DERAILING POSITION".  Crew member will 
confirm the message with Engineer in accordance with GCOR 6.1.1 (Verbal 
Communication). 
• Movement may proceed once a green aspect is received.  
• Derail will realign to derailing position when movement clears the track between OS 
signs, and a set timer has expired. 
• Once aligned to derailing position red aspect will be displayed and location will transmit 
message "3.8 HUMBOLDT DERAIL IS IN DERAILING POSITION" Crew member will
GENERAL ORDER NO. C-15 
 PAYNESVILLE SUBDIVISION 
 MAY 13, 2025 
 
CONFIDENTIAL 
Page 4 of 4 
 
confirm derail message with Engineer in accordance with GCOR 6.1.1 (Verbal 
Communication). 
Although it is not necessary in normal train movements, touch tone number #0382 using 
radio channel AAR (094-094) will throw switch into derailing position. 
• Crew member can transmit touch tone number #0389 to query position of switch.  
• If message is NOT heard after the rear of train clears track between OS signs within 1 
minute, movement will come to stop and crew member will hand operate the power switch 
derail back to derailing position in accordance with GCOR 8.20 or an understandin g has 
been reached between other employees that they will line the power switch derail back to 
derailing position. When no message is received, crew member will report this to the train 
dispatcher who will inform the communication center. If derail indicator light does not 
display green aspect, then the power derail must be operated by hand before proceeding. 
Hand operate the derail as follows: 
• Stop movement before passing OS sign for the derail 
• Unlock the switch lock securing pump handle 
• Place pump handle in receiver, toggle the directional selector, and pump switch to the 
desired position 
 
If indicator light displays Red, Flashing Red, Double Red, White, or no indication is 
displayed, stop movement before passing OS sign. Switch must then be hand operated 
per GCOR 9.13.1 (Hand Operation of Dual Control Switches), permission from control 
operator is not necessary to hand operate this switch.  
• Only single Red – indicates switch in derailing position 
• Green over Red – lined for non-derailing position, with OS reading occupied 
• Red over Red – lined for derailing position, with OS reading occupied 
• Flashing Red – indicates switch is out of correspondence (OOC) 
• White – Switch has been placed in Maintenance Mode 
 
Maintenance of Way movements must place switch in maintenance mode by use of MOW 
lock box on switch stand before passing ‘Begin OS’ sign; then hand operate the switch as 
outlined above for their movements.   Maintenance of Way movements must be clear of 
‘End OS’ sign location before deselecting MOW lockout box to return switch to power for 
remote operation.

METRA  
SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS  
 
General Code of Operating Rules Eighth Edition Applies  
 
Personnel operating on Metra trackage using the CORA Guide will be governed by the rules listed in the GCOR section 
of the CORA Guide EXCEPT as modified by this section of the  Guide. Where the Metra Special Instructions section 
adds to or changes the GCOR rules, the words "Addition:" or "Change:" preface the additional rules or new 
wording. All portions of the rule that are not referenced remain unchanged from the GCOR section of the CORA 
Guide.   
Rules and instructions in the Metra section may have been modified to suit the purposes of this publication. This section 
must not be used by Metra train, engine and yard service personnel.   
GLOSSARY Addition:   
Abbreviations    
BDA........................…… Blocking Devices Applied    
BDR......................…….. Blocking Devices Removed  
BV............................….. Beverly   
JA............................…... Joliet   
PS………………………. Passenger Station   
Sub Dist......................... Sub District   
SW................................. Southwest   
Employee Train Schedule    
A publication containing the schedules of passenger trains which will designate direction, number, and 
movement. The Employee Train Schedule does not convey authority.    
Enhanced Focus Crossover Location   
A power-operated crossover location, designated in Sub District Special Instructions, requiring heightened awareness 
of crew members on trains consisting entirely of passenger equipment due to the difference  between the maximum 
authorized speed and the speed restriction through the diverging route of the crossover(s).   
Key Train   
Train carrying specified numbers of loaded railcars, trailers, or containers of hazardous materials.  
Men or Equipment    
A term referring to Roadway Workers and their related equipment.  Roadway Workers will be identified by fluorescent 
orange work wear with reflective striping.   
Passenger Train    
A train shown in the Employee Train Schedule.  
Schedule Time     
The time shown in the Employee Train Schedule.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 2 © CORA 2024
METRA  
1.47 DUTIES OF CREW MEMBERS Addition:   
Observe and Call Signals   
If the engineer is solely occupying the control compartment of a train, they must verbally communicate to a promoted 
crew member on the train the name or aspect of:   
• All absolute signals displaying a signal aspect less favorable than Rule 9.1.5 – Clear.   
• All signals governing the approach to absolute signals displaying a signal aspect less favorable than Rule   
9.1.5 – Clear.   
• All signals displaying Rule 9.1.4 – Approach or a less favorable signal indication where the Maximum   
Authorized Speed is greater than 30 MPH.   
• The prescribed speed through the turnout of an Enhanced Focus Crossover Location when:   
-  The signal in advance of that location displays Rule 9.1.7 – Approach Diverging or Rule 9.1.11 –  
Diverging Approach Diverging.   
   or   
-  It is determined that the train will make a diverging movement at that location.    
     
Each communication must be acknowledged by the crew member on the train. If the crew member fails to acknowledge 
the communication, the engineer must determine the reason for failure to acknowledge prior  to leaving the next 
scheduled passenger stop. Communication must include:   
•  Train identification.   
•  Name or Aspect of the signal.   
•  Location of the signal.   
•  Track designation if in multiple track territory.  
If the engineer fails to properly control the speed of the train, the crew member must immediately 
communicate with the engineer. If necessary, the crew member must stop the train.   
If the next signal in advance changes to a more favorable indication, the engineer must communicate the change to a 
crew member on the train.   
If the radio is inoperative, the communication must be made by intercom, public address system or in person.   
Verbal communication is required. Use of the 
buzzer or communicating signal is prohibited.  
 
These requirements do not apply in territories where specified in Sub District Special Instructions.  
2.21 ELECTRONIC DEVICES Addition:   
Employees operating on Metra trackage will be governed by the Rule in effect on the railroad they are employed 
by.   
4.3 TIMETABLE CHARACTERS Addition:  
A ....................................….. Ticket Clerk   
B .....................................…. General Order Board  
D .....................................…. Passenger Stop   
F.......................................… Facsimile Machine   
H.......................................… Control Point   
J.......................................… Junction   
M......................................… Manual Interlocking   
P.......................................… Telephone    
R.......................................… Radio   
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 3 © CORA 2024
METRA  
S.......................................… Siding    
T.......................................… Turntable or Wye   
X ......................................… Crossover   
X(2)...................................…Multiple Crossovers  
Y.......................................… Yard   
 
4.4 EMPLOYEE TRAIN SCHEDULE Addition:   
Schedules of passenger trains are shown in the Employee Train Schedule. Employees concerned or 
whose duties are affected by the movement of these trains must have a copy in their possession while on  duty. The 
Employee Train Schedule does not convey authority.   
Sunday  schedules  are  in  effect  New  Year’s  Day,  Memorial  Day,  Independence  Day,  Labor  Day, 
Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day.   
4.4.1 SCHEDULE TIME Addition:   
Where one time is shown, it is the leaving time; except at terminating stations, it is the arriving time . Where two times 
are shown, they are the arriving and leaving times.   
Times shown in shading are approximate times which do not restrict train movement .  Times not shaded  indicate a 
regular stop and trains must not leave ahead of these times .  At Flag Stops, trains will stop to  discharge passengers 
on notice to Conductor and to pick up passengers on station platform visible to the  Engineer.   
Except as otherwise provided, trains scheduled to receive, or discharge passengers must not leave the point where 
passengers are received or discharged before the leaving times shown.   
Schedule times shown for Empty Equipment Trains are for information only . Empty Equipment Trains may operate in 
advance of these times.   
4.4.2 SCHEDULE SYMBOLS Addition:   
The following symbols when placed in the schedule column of the Employee Train Schedule indicate:  
A..................................…. Arrive   
L...................................…. Leave   
Y...................................… Arrive or Leave Yard   
s...................................…. Regular Stop   
f....................................…. Flag Stop   
DH................................…. Empty Equipment Train  
5.4.1 TEMPORARY RESTRICTIONS Addition:   
The second paragraph of GCOR Rule 5.4.1 (Temporary Restrictions) does not apply on Metra Sub Districts.  
5.4.2 DISPLAY OF YELLOW FLAG Change:    
A. Restriction Is in Effect   
One Mile Ahead of Restricted Area: Yellow flags warn trains to restrict movement because of track conditions 
or structures. To make sure train movement is restricted at the right location, employees must  display a yellow flag 1 
mile before the restricted area.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 4 © CORA 2024
METRA  
Less than One Mile Ahead of Restricted Area:  When the restricted area is close to a terminal, junction  or another 
area, employees will display the yellow flag less than 1 mile before the restricted area. This information will also be 
included in the track bulletin, track warrant, track permit or general order.     
When the maximum authorized speed is 35 MPH or less over the entire Sub District, low profile yellow flags will be 
displayed between the rails at the limits of the restriction.   
Once the Train Reaches the Restricted Area.  The speed specified by track warrant, track bulletin, track  permit, 
general order or radio speed restriction must not be exceeded until the rear if the train clears the  restricted area.   
B. Restriction is Not in Effect   
When a yellow flag is displayed, and the restriction is not specified by a track bulletin, track warrant, track  permit or 
general order, once the train is 1 mile beyond the yellow flag, crew members must:   
1.   Continue moving the train but at a speed not exceeding 10 MPH.   
2. Resume speed only after the rear of the train has:   
a. Passed a green flag.   
or   
b. Traveled 3 miles beyond the yellow flag and the train dispatcher has verified that no track bulletin   
or track warrant is in effect specifying a temporary speed restriction at that location.   
5.4.3 DISPLAY OF YELLOW-RED FLAG Change:   
A. Restriction Is In Effect:   
One Mile Ahead of Restricted Area. Yellow-red flags warn a train to be prepared to stop because of men or equipment. 
To make sure the train is prepared to stop at the right location; employees must display a yellow-red flag 1 mile before 
the restricted area.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Less Than One Mile Ahead of Restricted Area.  When the restricted area is close to a terminal, junction  or another 
area, employees will display the yellow-red flag less than 1 mile before the restricted area. This information will also be 
included in the track bulletin, track permit, track warrant or general order.   
When the maximum authorized speed is 35 MPH or less over the entire Sub District, low profile yellow-red flags will be 
displayed between the rails as indicated above.     
Addition:    
Yellow-red flags may be displayed from one hour before to one hour after a track bulletin Form B is in effect. During the 
hour before and the hour after the Form B is in effect, an attempt must be made to contact the  employee in charge 
(EIC) when Yellow-red flags are displayed. The (EIC) may provide instructions to proceed without restriction, 
specifying the track bulletin number. If contact with the (EIC) is not established, Rule 5.4.3B (Restriction Is Not in Effect) 
will apply.    
The display of yellow-red flags as described does not extend the authorized working limits beyond the times listed on 
the track bulletin Form B.   
 
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 5 © CORA 2024
METRA  
B. Restriction Is Not In Effect    
When a yellow-red flag is displayed, and the restriction is not specified by a track bulletin, track permit, track warrant or 
general order, crew members must be prepared to stop short of a red flag 1 mile beyond the  yellow-red flag. If a red 
flag is displayed, proceed as outlined in Rule 5.4.7 (Display of Red Flag). If no red  flag is displayed:   
 
1. Move at restricted speed.   
2. Increase speed only after:  
a. A crew member has received permission from the employee in charge.   
or   
b. The leading wheels of movement are 3 miles beyond the yellow-red flag, and the train dispatcher  
has verified that no track bulletin protecting men or equipment is in effect at that location.   
Addition:   
Yellow-red flags will not be displayed:  
• When roadway workers and/or equipment are working under track and time, track permit or foul time.    or   
• In advance of orange working limits banners displayed by Flagmen.   
5.4.5 DISPLAY OF GREEN FLAG Addition:   
When the maximum authorized speed is 35 MPH or less over the entire Sub District, low profile green flags will be 
displayed between the rails at the end of the temporary restriction.   
5.4.7 DISPLAY OF RED FLAG Addition:   
When the maximum authorized speed is 35 MPH or less over the entire Sub District, low profile red flags  will be 
displayed between the rails at the limits of track bulletins Form B and Form D when the employee in charge is a Foreman.   
Displayed Between Rails. Add new last sentence reading:   
Low profile red flags are not required to be removed before the train may proceed.  
5.5 PERMANENT SPEED SIGNS Change first paragraph to read:   
Permanent speed signs, where installed, will be placed 1,320 feet in advance of permanent speed restrictions.  
Signs may be placed to the left or right of main track as viewed by an approaching train. Numbers on the face of 
these signs indicate the highest speed permitted over the limits of the restriction.   
Addition:   
Passenger Train Crossover Speed Signs   
Passenger train crossover speed signs will be placed 1,320 feet in advance of power -operated crossover  switches 
between main tracks in territory where the Maximum Authorized Speed or Permanent Speed Restrictions for 
passenger trains are greater than 30 MPH . Signs will be placed on the field side of outside  main tracks as viewed by 
an approaching train. The number on the face of these signs indicates the highest speed permitted for trains consisting 
entirely of passenger equipment through the diverging route of the  crossover.   
Crew members of trains consisting entirely of passenger equipment making diverging movement through the crossover 
must not exceed the speed shown on the crossover speed sign until the rear of the train has cleared the crossover.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 6 © CORA 2024
METRA  
5.8.1 RINGING ENGINE BELL Addition:   
Engine bell must be rung when approaching and passing:  
• Station platforms at passenger stations.   
• Roadway Workers working on or near the tracks.   
    
5.8.2 SOUNDING WHISTLE Addition:    
Whistle signal 5.8.2(7) must be sounded, regardless of any whistle prohibitions, when meeting or passing  the head 
end or rear end of a train that is:   
• Stopping, standing, or starting from a station platform, except at downtown Chicago terminals or stations   
with high level platforms.   
   or    
• At or near a grade crossing.   
5.8.4 WHISTLE QUIET ZONES Addition:   
"No Whistle" roadway signs will be placed 1,320 feet in advance of these crossings.  
5.9.1 DIMMING HEADLIGHT Addition:   
Except when the engine is approaching and passing over a public crossing at grade, including authorized  pedestrian 
crosswalks, the headlight may be dimmed when approaching and passing the head end of a train only at night.   
5.9.5 DISPLAYING DITCH LIGHTS Addition:   
When contacting roadway workers, advise them when ditch lights are not working properly. Also advise crew members 
of the failure. Employees must advise trains when ditch lights are observed not working properly.   
5.17 ORANGE WORKING LIMITS BANNERS Add New Rules:   
5.17.1 Display of Orange Working Limits Banner   
Orange working limits banners are displayed to establish working limits, protecting roadway workers and/or equipment, 
at locations where trains or on-track equipment must stop. The orange working limits banner is made of orange material 
with the words "WORKING LIMITS" stenciled on it.   
A. Main Tracks and Controlled Sidings   
Orange working limits banners can be displayed on main tracks or controlled sidings at or within the limits  of the 
following authorities:   
• Form B Track Bulletin   
• Form D Track Bulletin   
• Joint Track and Time   
or   
• Joint Track Permit   
At or within the limits of the above authorities, trains or on-track equipment approaching an orange working limits banner 
must stop short of the orange working limits banner and not proceed unless the employee in  charge gives verbal 
permission, including the milepost location of the orange working limits banner. If multiple orange working limits 
banners are displayed, trains must be advised of the mile post location of  each orange working limits banner before 
entering the limits. If verbal permission is received before the train or on track equipment stops, the train or on-track 
equipment may pass the orange working limits banners without stopping.   
Within current of traffic, banners must be placed in both directions on each track affected.  
B.  Other than Main Tracks and Controlled Sidings   
Orange working limits banners can be displayed on other than main tracks or controlled sidings.  
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 7 © CORA 2024
METRA  
On other than main tracks or controlled sidings, trains or on-track equipment approaching an orange working 
limits banner must stop short of the orange working limits banner and not proceed unless the employee in charge 
gives verbal permission. If verbal permission is received before the train or on-track equipment stops, the train or on-
track equipment may pass the orange working limits banner without stopping.   
5.17.2 BANNER LOCATION   
Banners will be displayed only on the track affected.  
They must be displayed to the right of the track as viewed from approaching train, except in multiple track  territory or 
where sidings are adjacent to main track(s), they will be placed on the field side of outside tracks.  Banners will be 
displayed in this manner unless otherwise specified by track bulletin, track warrant, special instructions, or general order.  
When banners are displayed beyond the first rail of an adjacent track, the  banners will not apply to the track on which 
the train is moving.   
When banners are displayed for a main track or controlled siding where no Form B or Form D Track Bulletin, no Track and 
Time or no Track Permit is in effect, trains must stop short of the banner, if consistent with  good train handling.  After 
stopping, the train must proceed at restricted speed until the head end is 1 mile beyond the banner. The location of the 
banner must be reported to the train dispatcher.   
6.13.1 CONDITIONAL YARD LIMITS Add New Rule:    
Conditional Yard Limits, designated by Conditional Yard Limit signs, may be established on specified main track(s) 
between designated points:    
• By track bulletin or general order for hours and/or days indicated using the following format:   
"Conditional Yard Limits are in effect on the (Name) Sub District between MP ____ (or Location) and MP  
____ (or Location) on (Track or Tracks) from (Time and Date) until (Time and Date)."   
   or   
• Verbally by the train dispatcher in an emergency, when authorized by the Superintendent, using the    
   following words to notify each movement before it enters the Conditional Yard Limits:   
"Conditional Yard Limits are in effect on the (Name) Sub District between MP ____ (or Location) and MP ____ (or 
Location) on (Track)."   
The notification must be repeated to and confirmed by the train dispatcher with "That is correct."  
All movements within Conditional Yard Limits must be made in accordance with the provisions of Rule 6.13 (Yard Limits) 
and movements must not be made against the current of traffic unless authorized by the train dispatcher, who must first 
ensure that no opposing movements have been authorized.    
6.30 RECEIVING OR DISCHARGING PASSENGERS Addition:   
When a passenger train is receiving or discharging passengers, a freight train must not pass on an adjacent track.   
6.32.2 Automatic Warning Device Malfunction Message Change Item B and Item C to read:  
B: The Conductor and Engineer must have copies of the Automatic Warning Device Malfunction Message for each Sub 
District on which they will operate and must complete the "To" and "Date" lines prior to departure.     
When notified that automatic warning devices are malfunctioning, copy the issued Bulletin Number on the  appropriate 
line.  Mark Box(es) and Item(s) for the Line(s) on the form as instructed and be governed by the preprinted instructions 
for the Item(s) marked.     
Instructions must be repeated to and confirmed by the transmitting employee with "That is Correct", their  initials, and 
the time.  When confirmed by the transmitting employee mark the transmitting employee’s initials and time in the 
"That is Correct" Box(es).    
The Automatic Warning Device Malfunction Message may not be copied by the employee at the controls  of a moving 
engine. Restrictions remain in effect on subsequent trips unless voided.   
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 8 © CORA 2024
METRA  
ITEM 1 – Devices have Activation Failure or are Disabled.    
Stop before fouling the crossing.  After a crew member is on the ground at the crossing to warn traffic, proceed over 
the crossing as directed by that crew member. Then proceed at normal speed.    
ITEM 2 – Devices are Malfunctioning, or Equipped Flagger is present providing warning for one direction 
of approaching traffic.    
Proceed over the crossing not exceeding 15mph without stopping until head end of the train completely  occupies the 
crossing, then proceed at normal speed.     
ITEM 3 – Equipped Flaggers are present providing warning for all directions of traffic.   
Trains that receive an Item No. 3 may proceed over the crossing at normal speed without stopping.  
Item No. 3 Automatic Warning Device Malfunction Messages will be issued under General Information on  the Daily 
Operating Bulletin.     
BARRICADED CROSSING – Crossing devices are out of service and the crossing is barricaded and 
closed to vehicular traffic.   
Trains that receive a Barricaded Crossing bulletin may proceed over the crossing at normal speed   
without stopping.     
Barricaded Crossing bulletins will be issued under Barricaded Crossings on the Daily Operating Bulletin .    9.1 
SIGNAL ASPECTS AND INDICATIONS Addition:   
Block or interlocking signals which govern the approach to interlockings or control points are identified by  two orange 
retro-reflective stripes.   
9.5 WHERE STOP MUST BE MADE Change third bullet to read:   
• Report it to and be governed by instructions of the train dispatcher.  
9.15 TRACK PERMITS Addition:   
On tracks designated in the timetable, a track permit will authorize:  
• A train to occupy the main track or tracks between specific points.   
   or   
• A train to operate against the current of traffic outside yard limits.   
• Track cars or employees to occupy the main track or outside CTC or interlocking limits.  
 The track permit must be issued by a designated control operator under the direction of the train dispatcher. Within the 
limits, movements may be made only in the direction(s) specified.   
A train must obtain authority to pass a controlled signal displaying Stop indication to enter track permit limits.  Within 
track permit limits a train, after stopping, may pass a signal displaying Stop indication at restricted speed without 
further authority, except when signal governs movement at an interlocking.   
Track permit Box 5 can be issued in any main track territory to convey information concerning:  
• Track bulletins in effect when trains are not required or are unable to secure a track warrant.  
• Unforeseen speed or track restrictions.   
The provisions of Rule 9.15.1 (Issuing Track Permits) and Rule 9.15.2 (Clearing Track Permits) do not apply to a 
track permit issued only to convey information concerning track bulletins or track restrictions which does not grant 
authority.   
 
 
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 9 © CORA 2024
METRA  
More than One Track Permit Add:   
Before a joint track permit is issued to trains with machines, track cars or employees, the employee in charge of 
the machines, track cars or employees must grant permission. When a joint track permit is issued to trains with machines, 
track cars or employees, trains must not enter the limits unless instructed by the employee in charge of the machines, 
track cars or employees and that employee directs all movements.   
When track permit is issued to trains with other trains, contact between trains is not required.  
10.3 TRACK AND TIME Addition to Item C:   
Upon request, the holder of track and time may release a portion of the original track and time limits to the  control 
operator.  The holder must be clear of the portion of the limits being released before releasing that  portion of the 
authority. The control operator will convey the change to the holder using the following words:   
    
"Track and time (number) now reads between (location) and (location)."   
The holder must not re-enter the released portion unless new track and time authority is granted.  
10.3.3 JOINT TRACK AND TIME Addition:   
Joint track and time must not be issued to trains with machines, track cars or employees unless the employee 
in charge of the machines, track cars or employees grants permission. When joint track and time is granted to trains with 
machines, track cars or employees, trains must not enter the limits unless instructed by the employee in charge of the 
machines, track cars or employees and that employee directs all movements.   
When joint track and time is granted to trains with other trains, contact between trains is not required.  
10.3.4 TRACK AND TIME ACKNOWLEDGMENT Change first paragraph to read:   
Track and time authority must be recorded and repeated to the control operator.  The control operator will  check the 
repeated information and, if correct, will say "OK" and give the time and his name . The employee will record the "OK" 
time and the control operator’s name on the track and time form and repeat them to the control operator.  Track and time 
authority is not in effect until the "OK" time has been recorded, repeated  and acknowledged.   
14.0 Rules Applicable Only Within Track Warrant Control (TWC) Limits    
Entire Chapter Does Not Apply on Metra Operated Districts. Any reference to Track Warrant is replaced with Daily 
Operating Bulletin (DOB).    
15.0 TRACK BULLETIN RULES Addition: TRACK 
BULLETIN FORMS   
Form A -  Temporary speed restriction In Effect.   
Form B -  Protection of men and equipment fouling a main track or other tracks designated in Special  
Instructions.   
Form C -  Sound whistle signal 5.8.2(8) and ring engine bell through the limits during the time specified.   
Form D -  May be used to remove a main track from service or to provide other information affecting train   
movements or safety.   
15.1 – Track Bulletins under "Receipt and Comparison of Track Bulletins addition:  
Daily Operating Bulletin (DOB)   
All Trains and Employee in Charge must have a current DOB in their possession unless authorized by the train 
dispatcher.  Daily Operating Bulletin limits (DOB) are designated in the System Special Instructions.   
A DOB will take effect at 03:01 and remain in effect for 24 hours unless made void by the train dispatcher.   
 
 
 
 
Metra CORA Update 2024 - 001  METRA - 10 © CORA 2024

If a train is operating when a new DOB takes effect, the train may continue to operate with the prior DOB.  A crew

18.0 Rules Applicable only in Positive Train Territory (PTC Active Trains)   
18.1 Positive Train Control Territory:   
PTC territory is specified in special instructions. A train must not be operated in PTC territory if the controlling 
locomotive is not equipped with an operable PTC system unless otherwise authorized by rule,  special instructions, or 
the train dispatcher. Only PTC qualified operating employees are authorized to operate PTC enabled equipment 
within PTC territory.

18.2 Taking Charge of PTC Equipped Trains   
When taking charge of a train in PTC territory, or before entering PTC territory, the engineer must confirm:  
1.   The PTC circuit breaker and cut out switches are in the cut in position.   
- If a PTC circuit breaker or cut out switch is found in the off position, notify the train Dispatcher   
for instructions.   
- Crews are prohibited from turning off PTC circuit breakers unless authorized by the train  
Dispatcher.   
2.   The PTC system on the controlling locomotive is initialized.   
- If the system fails to initialize, notify the train dispatchers for instructions.   
- If the system fails to initialize at a train’s initial PTC Terminal, the train may depart (without   
passengers) and proceed to the next forward designated repair point. Movement must be governed by rule 18.12. 
(movements with inoperative PTC System). These restrictions do not  apply if the failing locomotive is repaired or 
replaced.   
3.   Departure test is performed at the train’s initial terminal or when prompted by the PTC system. When an engineer 
is relieved before a trip is completed, the PTC system must be logged off before the relieving engineer takes charge of 
the train.   
18.7 Comparison of PTC Display Information   
After each Initialization, crew members on the controlling locomotive must compare information such as track 
bulletins, restrictions, and authorities shown on the PTC display with those in their possession.    
18.9 Use of Restricted Mode   
Restricted mode must be turned on before performing the following work events:  
• Switching,   
• Pickups or setouts,   
• Headroom moves,   
• Entering form D limits (once proper authority is obtained).  
After the work event has been completed, turn off restricted mode.  
18.12 Movements with inoperative PTC System   
Immediately notify the train dispatcher when the controlling locomotive’s PTC system becomes inoperative, except when 
operating where PTC is suspended by Mandatory Directive. When the PTC System on the  controlling locomotive 
inoperative when enroute, unless otherwise restricted, the following speeds will govern:   
In non-signaled territory, or when operating against the current of traffic in Rule 9.14 (Movement with the current of 
traffic) territory:

• All other trains……………..............................................................................................40MPH   
     
In signaled territory:   
• Freight trains transporting one or more loaded cars containing TIH/PIH…..................40MPH   
• Freight trains not transporting loaded cars containing TIH/PIH…………………………49MPH   
• Passenger trains……………………………………………………………………………...59MPH

20.2 KEY TRAINS AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS   
Employees who in any way handle hazardous materials must have a copy of the instructions for handling  these 
materials.  Employees must be familiar with and comply with these instructions or regulations.    
Before movement of trains containing such materials are authorized to occupy Metra tracks, the conductor, or other 
qualified employee, must notify the train dispatcher or control operator.   
Any incident involving a potential release of hazardous material must be immediately reported to the train  dispatcher 
or control operator .  Extreme caution must be exercised to ensure passengers and employees  are not exposed to 
hazardous materials.   
Trains containing the following minimum quantities of the materials specified shall not be left unattended  on Metra 
Main Tracks or Sidings under any circumstances:   
• Five or more tank car loads of any one or any combination of materials poisonous by inhalation as 
defined in 49CFR 171.8 and including anhydrous ammonia (UN 1005) and ammonia solutions (UN 
3318).   
  or   
• 20 rail car loads or intermodal portable tank loads of any one or any combination of materials listed   
above, or any Division 2.1 flammable gas, Class 3 flammable liquid or combustible liquid, Class 1.1 or 1.2 explosive, 
or hazardous substance listed in 49 CFR 173.31(f)(2).   
Unattended means equipment left standing and unmanned in such a manner that the brake system, either hand or air 
brakes, may not be readily controlled by a crew member or qualified person.

BENSENVILLE YARD CONSTRUCTION UPDATE 
 
Bensenville will be under continuous construction over the next couple of years and we will be  issuing out 
Superintendent Notices to keep the employees updated on areas that they will need to be cautious around.  
 
Effective Monday, June 27, 2024, Bensenville Yard will be going through extensive construction altering the 
layout of the yard.   
 
All employees & crews that are starting their shift, as well as crews entering the yard will be required to have 
a job briefing with the Yardmaster on duty to go over current changes and what to look out for.  
 
Crews are expected to be mindful of all the heavy machinery, contracted employees and semi -trucks that will 
be moving throughout Bensenville Yard. Do not get distracted and always remember to take the safe course.  
 
(June 27, 2024) – Construction updates as follows:  
 
CHANGES TO EXISTING TRACKS  
• PBD/PBA & PB2 – Will be shifted to the new alignment.  
• PB1 – Will be going out of service and removed completely.  
• PB3 & PB4 – Will continue to use the old lead for access on the West end.  
 
NEW CHANGES  
• New IMS Departure, Arrival, and IMS 1 will be in-service post-shutdown.  
• The new IMS Departure Track will tie into the A Lead.  
• The new IMS Arrival Track will tie into the West Yard Lead.

3. IHB MAIN LINE – CP IVANHOE – MODIFIED 5/15/2025:

7. TIMETABLE SPECIAL INSTRUCTION 2305 – SECURING UNATTENDED TRAINS AND CARS (GCOR 
7.6) – MODIFIED 12/13/2024: 
Effective 0600 12/13/2024, there have been multiple changes to the Gibson Auto Yard portion of Special 
Instruction 2305 on page 89 of IHB Timetable No.3: 
• Fourth row’s Quantity of Cars column has been modified to read, "3 or more" 
• Fifth row has been deleted (required 4 hand brakes for 4 cars). 
• Sixth row has been deleted. 
• The paragraph underneath the table has been replaced. 
The same changes have been made to page IHB-21 of the CORA Guide. Below is how the Gibson Auto 
Yard portion of Special Instruction 2305 will read after the modifications:  
 
GIBSON AUTO YARD 
A securement test is not required if equipment is secured with hand brakes according to the table below:  
 
Quantity of Cars Hand 
Brake(s) 
1 1

3 or more 3 
Inbound Trains 
Inbound train crews must job brief the West End Auto Yardmaster on radio channel 025 -025 or 095-095 
regarding how many hand brakes they applied to cars. 
 
Switching Operation 
Crews involved in switching operations must apply the hand brakes to the leading car(s) when shoving into a 
clear track. 
 
After a yard job involved in switching operations has completed all assigned work, a crew member must job 
brief with the West End Auto Yardmaster regarding which tracks they left cars in and stating quantity of hand 
brakes were applied per rule. The job briefing must take place on radio channel 095-095 or by calling 219-
989-4827. 
 
Yardmaster 
Yardmaster must document the hand brake information on their securement form after the job briefing has 
been completed. They must job brief all applicable employees on the securement status of each track.

10. TIMETABLE SPECIAL INSTRUCTION 2803 – FORM B SHEET – EIC RESPONSIBILITIES (GCOR 
15.2) – ADDED  7/23/2024: 
Effective 0600 7/23/2024, employees must make a note on page 114 of IHB Timetable No. 3, "See bulletin 
change dated 7/23/2024" and keep a copy of Timetable Special Instruction 2803 in their possession. Foreign 
line crews must make the same note on Page IHB-44 of the CORA Guide. Below is new rule Timetable 
Special Instruction 2803: 
 
2803   FORM B SHEET – EIC RESPONSIBILITIES (GCOR 15.2) 
1. When an EIC (employee in charge) has established on-track protection via Form B, they must record 
all movement instructions in the "IHB Form B Instructions" booklet prior to transmitting the movement 
related instructions via radio.  
2. After the movement instructions are recorded in the "IHB Form B Instructions" booklet, transmit the 
information to the train crew on the appropriate radio channel. 
3. After the train crew repeats the information correctly, the EIC must provide his/her initials and time to 
the train crew.  
4. Once the train has cleared the Form B limits, the EIC must mark the sheet with an "X" and have it 
available for inspection until the end of the following day. 
 
11. TIMETABLE SPECIAL INSTRUCTION 2804 – FORM B SHEET – CREW MEMBER 
RESPONSIBILITIES (GCOR 15.2) – ADDED  7/23/2024: 
Effective 0600 7/23/2024, employees must make a note on page 114 of IHB Timetable No. 3, "See bulletin 
change dated 7/23/2024" and keep a copy of Timetable Special Instruction 2804 in their possession. Foreign 
line crews must make the same note on Page IHB-44 of the CORA Guide. Below is new rule Timetable 
Special Instruction 2804: 
 
2804   FORM B SHEET – CREW MEMEBER RESPONSIBILITIES (GCOR 15.2) 
1. When an EIC (employee in charge) transmits Form B movement related instructions via radio, a 
crew member must copy the instructions on the "IHB Form B Sheet".  
2. Repeat the information back to the EIC after copying the movement related instructions. Record the 
EIC’s initials and time after the repeat is confirmed. 
3. Once the train has cleared the Form B limits, a crew member must mark the sheet with an "X" and 
have it available for inspection until the end of the employee’s shift. 
 
Note: Unless instructed otherwise by the EIC, if a train stops within the working limits the train crew must get 
permission on the restart before resuming movement. 
 
12. KANKAKEE LINE – MAP (PAGE 11) – MODIFIED 3/27/2024: 
Effective 0600 3/27/2024, a replacement page will be made available at all reporting locations for page 11 of

IFG - Remote Control Locomotives  
Remote Control Operations may be in use at IFG. Locomotive cab may not be occupied.  
 
Prior making any movements within IFG that will be in a location that has remote control zone, all 
movements must contact the Remote Control Assignment Operator by using radio channel 013-013 
to determine if there are any of the remote -control zones activated. Engineering employees that 
have work to perform in the area of the remote -control zones also have to determine if any zones 
are active.  
 
If you are unable to make contact with the Remote Control Assignment, contact Knoche Yardmaster 
or CPKC Console 1 Dispatcher to determine if there are any active zones.  
 
Active Zone:  
After receiving instruction from the CPKC Console 1 Dispatcher and there is an active zone or zones 
and the inbound train, outbound train, lite engine, or other assignment will come into contact with an 
active zone, the movement must contact the Remote-Control Operator (RCO) to be granted access 
into that remote control zone and follow any instructions given by the RCO. The Conductor on the 
inbound or outbound train will also document on the Delay Report the time that they entered the 
Remote-Control Zone and the time that they cleared the Remote-Control Zone.  
 
Once the movement is clear of the remote -control zone the RCO must be advised, including the 
position of any switches used within the zone.

Zone Two:  South End
